title: LeetLLM Concept Atlas
description: Reusable SVG symbols with source-backed briefs for explanatory diagrams and simulations.
reviewScope: Article metadata, headings and visual explanations; glossary definition leads, structural cues and selected full sections. Per-source basis records the actual scope. This catalog identifies visual opportunities; it is separate from a factual or editorial audit.

concepts.title: A/B experiment assignment and inference
concepts.meaning: Randomly assigns units to control and treatment, estimates an outcome difference, and quantifies uncertainty.
concepts.brief: Show stable unit assignment into two arms, a declared primary metric, observed counts and means, confidence interval, and a guardrail metric; optionally trace sample-ratio checks.
pitfalls: The randomization unit must match interference and product exposure assumptions.
Statistical significance and practical value are separate decisions.

concepts.title: Accelerator dataflow map
concepts.meaning: Data moves from device memory into local tiles, through compute, and across peer links when needed.
concepts.brief: Trace a working tile from device memory into on-chip local storage, through a compute engine, then over a peer link when the workload requires another device. Mark the owner and capacity boundary at each stage.
pitfalls: Capacity and bandwidth belong to specific memory levels and owners.
Peer exchange may route over a shared link or host staging; measure the actual topology.

sourceRefs.title: Accelerator Architecture Field Guide
headings: Memory paths: capacity belongs to an owner
Interconnect topologies: count exchanges, then measure the route

concepts.title: Retrieval access filter
concepts.meaning: A trusted predicate that limits retrieval candidates by caller, tenant, version, or other product rules before evidence reaches later stages.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Three document cards approach a gate with small tenant, date, and access tags. One eligible card passes toward a magnifying lens; two denied cards stop before it. Use green for passed eligibility, red for blocked records, and cyan for the active path.
pitfalls: Place the gate before prompt packing and generation, not after.
Do not draw the filter as a relevance score or as a guarantee that matching text supports an answer.
Missing or stale authorization data should visibly fail closed.

concepts.title: Authorization gate
concepts.meaning: A trusted permission check admits only records the authenticated principal may read.

concepts.title: Activation functions
concepts.meaning: Adds a nonlinear transformation between affine neural-network layers.
concepts.brief: Build a small coordinate-plane SVG with selectable sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, and GELU curves; align each curve with its input and output values and mark saturation or the ReLU kink.
pitfalls: Curve shape is a local mathematical property, not a complete explanation of network behavior.
Show the actual axes and domain.

concepts.title: Active learning frontier
concepts.meaning: Uncertain examples near a model boundary are selected for human labeling.
concepts.brief: Plot unlabeled cases near a decision boundary, select a subset with an explicit acquisition rule, route it to annotation, then update and independently evaluate.
pitfalls: Uncertainty sampling can over-select noisy or out-of-distribution examples.
Reviewer data and final holdout labels need separate access controls.

sourceRefs.title: Data Labeling and Human Feedback
headings: Select cases that might teach something new

concepts.title: Adapter
concepts.meaning: A small trainable module added to a larger pretrained model.

sourceRefs.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Prompting: A Practical Guide

concepts.title: Adapter residency
concepts.meaning: A capacity hierarchy that moves task adapters among GPU, CPU, and storage tiers while a shared base model stays loaded.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Keep one large base-model block resident beside a small adapter chip. Show hot adapters in GPU slots, warm adapters on CPU, and cold adapters in a store. A single promotion arrow and LRU eviction path show residency changes.
pitfalls: Do not imply the full base model reloads on each adapter switch.
Adapter identity can affect cached KV state.
A small adapter file does not mean zero impact on GPU concurrency.

sourceRefs.title: Multi-Tenant LLM Platform
headings: Keep adapter residency separate from permission

concepts.title: Agent recovery state
concepts.meaning: A timed-out action is verified before a safe retry or operator handoff.
concepts.brief: Persist one operation key and approved payload before dispatch. After timeout, query the external system with that key; retry only when idempotency and reconciliation rules allow it.
pitfalls: A timeout does not prove a remote write failed.
An idempotent retry must reuse its operation identity.

sourceRefs.title: Agent Reliability, Recovery & Human Approval
headings: Lose the reply after a real local commit

concepts.title: AI app contract
concepts.meaning: A request passes input validation and trusted-fact checks before an uncertain model answer can affect a decision.

concepts.title: Algorithm growth
concepts.meaning: Logarithmic, linear, and quadratic operation counts diverge as input size increases.

concepts.title: Approval-bound action
concepts.meaning: A human decision bound to the exact proposed effect, policy, target revision, and validity window.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Draw an immutable action card with target, revision, and scope chips; place a reviewer mark and a small lock over the card digest. A changed amount or revision should visibly create a second card rather than editing the approved one.
pitfalls: A reviewer mark on a general request is not approval of later-edited arguments.
Approval expires and does not itself guarantee the effect succeeded.
Keep the action digest and resulting execution receipt distinct.

sourceRefs.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
headings: Persist, retry, and resume by semantics

concepts.title: Approval receipt
concepts.meaning: A recorded human decision is bound to one exact action, version, and set of preconditions.

concepts.title: Assistant loss mask
concepts.meaning: Supervised fine-tuning can score assistant targets while keeping user prompts as conditioning context.
concepts.brief: Color prompt tokens separately from assistant targets and place loss markers only beneath assistant targets.
pitfalls: A loss mask controls target positions; it does not remove prompt context.

concepts.title: Attention
concepts.meaning: A token combines information from other tokens using learned weights.

sourceRefs.title: DeepSeek V4: Facts, Claims, and Fit
Run Qwen3.6 Locally with llama.cpp and Unsloth GGUF

concepts.title: Audit receipt
concepts.meaning: Evidence of actor, identity, policy, evidence, versions, and outcome.
concepts.brief: Receipt links actor, time, policy/model versions, evidence hashes, outcome.
pitfalls: Minimize private raw payloads.

sourceRefs.title: AI Lab System Design Interview
headings: Prompt 1: model gateway for enterprise teams

concepts.title: Autoregressive generation loop
concepts.meaning: Produces a sequence by selecting one next token conditioned on the prompt and prior generated tokens.
concepts.brief: Show prompt tokens entering prefill, last-position logits flowing through a sampler, one selected token appending to the stream, and KV state reused on the next decode step.
pitfalls: Future tokens are generated sequentially in this loop.
Sampling settings alter the distribution and do not guarantee answer quality.

concepts.title: Autoscaling control loop
concepts.meaning: A controller that converts measured demand into desired replicas and admits only capacity that is scheduled, loaded, and healthy.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Build a circular loop from queue/latency gauge to controller to replica stack and readiness check. Add a small second node-provisioning branch for pending GPU pods. Only the green ready marker connects to a traffic arrow.
pitfalls: Replica count alone does not prove usable GPU capacity.
Pod and node autoscalers own different resources.
Scaling on utilization can miss queue-age or deadline pressure.

concepts.title: Backpressure
concepts.meaning: A capacity signal that slows, pauses, or rejects new work while downstream workers drain admitted work.
concepts.brief: 16:9 simulation with a fast producer, bounded queue, and slower worker. Increase arrival rate until the queue fills, then show await or 429 with Retry-After returning upstream while admitted requests keep draining. Expose admitted, queued, rejected, and retry counts.
pitfalls: Buffering without a bound is not backpressure.
Do not stop already admitted healthy work when rejecting new arrivals.
Rate limits are policy caps; backpressure reflects current capacity.

sourceRefs.title: GPU Serving & Autoscaling
headings: When capacity can't arrive in time

concepts.title: Backpropagation graph
concepts.meaning: Moves derivatives backward through a computation graph and adds contributions where paths meet.
concepts.brief: Show a minimal forward DAG for two inputs sharing one intermediate value, place local derivatives on edges, then animate reverse adjoints and addition at the shared node.
pitfalls: The reverse pass computes vector-Jacobian products; it does not materialize a full Jacobian.
Distinguish a local derivative from the accumulated gradient.

concepts.title: Batch
concepts.meaning: A group of inputs scheduled for shared processing.

sourceRefs.title: How Decision Models Like Jev Work: AI Without the Paragraph
Run Gemma 4 with Ollama: Model Tags and Memory Requirements

concepts.title: Bayesian update
concepts.meaning: Combines a prior distribution with observed-data likelihood to form a posterior distribution.
concepts.brief: Animate a Beta prior over success probability, a binomial likelihood from observed successes and trials, and the normalized posterior; expose how additional evidence narrows or shifts uncertainty.
pitfalls: A posterior depends on the stated prior, data model, and sampling assumptions.
Do not depict a point estimate as the entire posterior.

concepts.title: Beam search tree
concepts.meaning: Two candidate paths remain bright while lower-scoring branches are pruned.

concepts.title: Benchmark evidence gap
concepts.meaning: A polished benchmark score is separated from a distinct production evaluation.
concepts.brief: Trace a score through its dataset, harness, contamination controls, metric, and uncertainty. Compare it with production evaluation for safety, retrieval, latency, and user impact.
pitfalls: Different tasks or harnesses make scores incomparable.
A high aggregate score can hide a critical failure slice.

sourceRefs.title: LLM Benchmarks & Limitations
headings: A score is only meaningful with its contract

concepts.title: Benchmark protocol
concepts.meaning: Versioned rules for task population, scoring, budget, and valid comparison.
concepts.brief: Boundary around benchmark tasks, harness, model snapshot, budget, and score.
pitfalls: Claims apply only to declared tasks and harness.

sourceRefs.title: Understanding SWE-bench
headings: Choose the benchmark before reading a score

concepts.title: Bit packing
concepts.meaning: Storing low-bit values together in compact machine words.

concepts.title: Boosted residual tree
concepts.meaning: A shallow correction tree targets the remaining errors after an earlier prediction.

concepts.title: Bounded queue
concepts.meaning: Finite-capacity queue with explicit backpressure under overload.
concepts.brief: At capacity, requests wait, reject, or shed while consumers drain.
pitfalls: Bounded memory does not guarantee low latency.

concepts.title: Broadcast axis
concepts.meaning: Broadcasting reuses dimensions whose size is one across compatible array axes.
concepts.brief: Build a tiny batch-by-token-by-feature tensor and track its shape through indexing, reduction, reshape, transpose, and broadcasting. Show each input's dimensions before an elementwise addition, align shapes from the trailing axes, and expand a size-one dimension across the compatible batch. Then reshape a toy attention tensor into batch, head, token, and head-width axes while preserving element counts. Use explicit axis labels and verify every displayed element from the numeric arrays.
pitfalls: Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right and permits equal sizes or a size of one.
A reduction removes the selected axis unless keepdims is requested.
Reshape preserves element order while transpose permutes axes.
Equal element counts do not imply that a reshape preserves semantic axis meaning.
Batch, token, head, and feature axes must be labeled consistently with the source operation.

concepts.title: Cache
concepts.meaning: Reusable intermediate data kept close to computation.

sourceRefs.title: Best AI Plans for OpenClaw in 2026
DeepSeek V4: Facts, Claims, and Fit
LLM Inference Engines Compared: vLLM, SGLang, Ollama & llama.cpp
Run Gemma 4 with Ollama: Model Tags and Memory Requirements
Run Qwen3.6 Locally with llama.cpp and Unsloth GGUF

concepts.title: Cache block
concepts.meaning: A page of token state with a valid region and an allocation boundary.

concepts.title: Canary rollout
concepts.meaning: A time-limited, partial exposure of a new release with predeclared metrics and stop rules before wider promotion.
concepts.brief: 16:9 diagram with stable and candidate release rails and a sticky subset of eligible users routed to the candidate. Animate exposure widening only after checks pass; on a stop signal route new requests back to stable and preserve evidence of the window.
pitfalls: Reversing the route does not undo irreversible side effects or shared-backend damage.
Canary traffic is user-visible; shadow traffic is not.
A passing window is evidence for that candidate, workload, and time window.

concepts.title: Causal attention mask
concepts.meaning: A causal mask lets each position attend to itself and earlier positions while blocking future tokens.
concepts.brief: Reveal a lower-triangular attention mask aligned to token order; each row reads only its prefix.
pitfalls: The diagonal is visible because a position may attend to itself.

concepts.title: Causal effect
concepts.meaning: Outcome contrast under two interventions for a defined population and estimand.
concepts.brief: Treatment/control assignment, outcomes, contrast, assumptions.
pitfalls: Correlation alone is not causal identification.

concepts.title: Causal graph patterns
concepts.meaning: Uses directed graphs to encode assumptions about causal relationships and adjustment.
concepts.brief: Create three side-by-side causal motifs: chain, fork/confounder, and collider. Highlight which variables to condition on for each question and optionally distinguish observation from intervention with a separate do marker.
pitfalls: A DAG encodes assumptions; observed correlation alone does not identify causal effects.
Conditioning on a collider can create an association.

concepts.title: Chat template and training data flow
concepts.meaning: Serializes conversational records into token streams and assigns loss to selected positions.
concepts.brief: Show structured role/content messages rendered into special tokens, tokenized, packed with boundaries, and paired with a loss mask that includes assistant targets while retaining prompt context.
pitfalls: Templates are tokenizer/model-specific serialization contracts.
Packed examples need attention isolation where required; loss masks and attention masks serve different jobs.

concepts.title: Circuit breaker
concepts.meaning: A dependency guard that admits calls while healthy, fails fast while open, and allows a limited recovery probe.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Use three connected state capsules in a loop: closed, open, and half-open. Add a small counter mark on the closed-to-open transition and exactly one probe arrow from half-open. A failure loops open; success returns closed.
pitfalls: The transition depends on health policy and time windows, not a physical switch.
Half-open admission is limited; it is not normal full traffic.
Circuit breakers handle dependency health, while backpressure handles local capacity.

concepts.title: Citation span
concepts.meaning: A traceable link from a specific answer claim to the source text and version that support it.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Show a short source excerpt with one highlighted line, a small locator pin, and a curved connector to a claim card. Attach a tiny version marker to the source side. Use one clear connector so the eye follows claim to evidence.
pitfalls: A citation reference does not prove the claim is supported or the source is current.
Do not use a medal, star, or checkmark as the main symbol.
Keep source and answer as separate objects.

concepts.title: Claim evidence link
concepts.meaning: Answer claims connect to specific source spans, with unsupported claims left unlinked.
concepts.brief: Split an answer into atomic claims and bind each to a source span. Keep support, contradiction, and missing-evidence outcomes separate from broader world factuality.
pitfalls: Text overlap does not establish entailment.
Evidence-supported wording may still be stale or unauthorized for the caller.

concepts.title: Classification boundary
concepts.meaning: A decision boundary separates regions where a classifier predicts different classes.
concepts.brief: Show two labeled point groups separated by a linear boundary in a feature plane; keep points near the margin visible.
pitfalls: Do not present a boundary as a probability calibration curve.

concepts.title: Classification confusion matrix
concepts.meaning: Counts predicted labels against true labels so each error type remains visible.
concepts.brief: Render an accessible 2×2 or multiclass grid with truth on rows and predictions on columns; animate one example into TP, FP, FN, or TN and keep denominators labeled.
pitfalls: Axis orientation differs across libraries; label both axes explicitly.
Accuracy alone hides class-specific error costs.

concepts.title: Collective reduce-scatter ownership
concepts.meaning: Matching tensor chunks reduce across ranks and each rank retains the chunk at its own index.
concepts.brief: Give four ranks four-element vectors. Reduce corresponding indices, move the completed chunks through a ring or tree schedule, and leave chunk r on rank r. Then optionally run all-gather to reconstruct the full vector everywhere. Keep rank order, communicator agreement, buffer offsets and stream completion visible.
pitfalls: Reduce-scatter leaves one reduced shard per rank; it does not leave the full tensor everywhere.
Every rank must call matching collectives in matching order with compatible arguments.
In-place reduce-scatter and all-gather use rank-offset shard locations, not automatically the buffer base.

sourceRefs.title: Deep Dive - NCCL
headings: Choose the operation from desired ownership

concepts.title: Collective routing
concepts.meaning: Rank-to-rank movement satisfying distributed ownership contracts.
concepts.brief: Ranks exchange token shards to expert owners via all-to-all then return results.
pitfalls: All-to-all differs from all-gather.

sourceRefs.title: Deep Dive - NCCL
headings: Choose the operation from desired ownership

concepts.title: Compiler ownership stack
concepts.meaning: Source code is compiled into packaged device images with architecture-specific ownership and target rules.
concepts.brief: Trace one CUDA source through host compilation and device compilation into virtual and architecture-specific device images inside an executable. Highlight the artifact and diagnostic owned by each stage.
pitfalls: A host executable may contain multiple device images; source text is not the packaged artifact.
PTX and native machine code expose different compilation stages.

sourceRefs.title: GPU Compilers and Kernel Languages
headings: `nvcc` packages host code with architecture-specific device images

concepts.title: Compute-optimal training allocation
concepts.meaning: Shows how a fixed compute budget can be allocated across model size, data, and later inference costs.
concepts.brief: Render a compute budget slider that trades parameters against training tokens, then overlays loss/quality curves and serving-cost constraints; compare a training-only optimum with a lifetime-cost choice.
pitfalls: Scaling-law fits are empirical within measured regimes and may not extrapolate across architectures or data regimes.
Keep training and lifetime inference costs separate.

concepts.title: Confidence interval
concepts.meaning: Range computed by a stated procedure to quantify sampling uncertainty.
concepts.brief: Show estimate, interval, and repeated-sampling intuition with assumptions.
pitfalls: Not a probability that this particular interval contains the parameter.

concepts.title: Conformal prediction and coverage
concepts.meaning: Calibrates a prediction set or interval using held-out nonconformity scores and a finite-sample rank.
concepts.brief: Sort calibration errors, mark the finite-sample quantile rank, then apply the threshold to new predictions. Show interval width and empirical hits across a stream of exchangeable test points.
pitfalls: The standard guarantee is marginal under exchangeability; it does not ensure exact conditional coverage in every subgroup.
Show the calibration/test split explicitly.

concepts.title: Conformal quantile
concepts.meaning: A calibration quantile sets a prediction interval whose empirical coverage can be checked on held-out examples.

concepts.title: Principle-guided critique
concepts.meaning: A written principle guides a model's critique and revision of its draft before the revised answer becomes a supervised target.
concepts.brief: Keep one request and policy boundary fixed. Animate a draft, a principle-specific critique, and a revised supervised target; then show a separate AI preference comparison and reward-learning phase. End with a red-team case and independent human audit.
pitfalls: The principle does not replace application authorization or access controls.
The critique is training scaffolding; the revised answer is the direct-answer supervised target.
AI feedback can share the model family’s blind spots and needs external evaluation.

concepts.title: Context curation
concepts.meaning: Many source records pass through selection and compression into a focused prompt.
concepts.brief: Start with a large incident record set. Apply selection and compression rules, preserve provenance, and isolate incompatible trust domains before assembling the working context.
pitfalls: Context engineering includes tool definitions and memory, not only retrieved documents.
Compression can remove qualifiers that change a policy meaning.

concepts.title: Context window budget
concepts.meaning: A finite window is divided among system, history, evidence, request, and output space.
concepts.brief: Allocate finite capacity across instructions, history, evidence, request, and reserved output. Test evidence position without treating a larger window as guaranteed recall.
pitfalls: Input and reserved output share the configured limit.
A prompt can fit yet bury or omit required evidence.

sourceRefs.title: Long Context Window Management
headings: First gate: can the prompt fit, and what does it cost?

concepts.title: Continued training stream
concepts.meaning: A pretrained model adapts to new domain text while replay examples can preserve selected general-language behavior.
concepts.brief: Mix domain and replay targets in a fixed token budget. Show the resulting weighted gradient on a shared parameter, then compare domain and general evaluation lanes across candidate checkpoints.
pitfalls: Choose replay ratios through domain and general-task evaluation under the intended token budget.
A token mixture matches the intended objective only when scored-token weighting is correct.
Lower domain perplexity alone does not establish a better downstream model.

concepts.title: Continuous batching
concepts.meaning: A serving schedule that admits new sequences into freed decode slots between generation steps.
concepts.brief: 16:9 timeline with GPU decode steps as columns and sequence rows. In a static batch, keep a finished sequence's cells empty until the longest sequence ends. In continuous batching, insert a waiting sequence into that slot at the next scheduling step. Show KV/cache capacity as a separate admission constraint.
pitfalls: This is not batching unrelated tokens into one semantic sequence.
A slot can be reused only when the prior request's state is safely retired.
Decode slots and available KV memory both constrain admission.

sourceRefs.title: GPU Serving & Autoscaling
headings: Static batches wait for the longest reply

sourceRefs.title: Multi-Tenant LLM Platform
headings: Give admitted tenants a bounded turn

concepts.title: Contrastive pair
concepts.meaning: Contrastive learning pulls matching examples together in embedding space and separates mismatched examples.
concepts.brief: Place an anchor near its positive pair and far from negatives; animate positive attraction and negative repulsion.
pitfalls: Distance encodes embedding similarity, not a causal relationship.

concepts.title: Convolution and receptive field
concepts.meaning: Applies a shared local filter across image positions and combines channels into feature maps.
concepts.brief: Slide a small weighted kernel over a grid, reveal each dot-product output, then stack layers and show how the effective receptive field grows. Let padding/stride alter output shape.
pitfalls: Padding adds boundary values and can create artificial edge evidence.
Keep filter weights and input values visible for worked examples.

concepts.title: Cross-encoder reranker
concepts.meaning: A second-stage model that jointly scores query and candidate text to improve ordering within an already retrieved shortlist.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Place a query strip and one candidate passage side by side entering a shared small scoring core, then emerge as a reordered candidate card. Add a faint stack behind it to signal that reranking operates on a shortlist. Keep the candidate boundary explicit.
pitfalls: A cross-encoder scores query-document pairs jointly; it does not search the entire corpus for every request.
Reranking does not grant access or establish citation support.
Avoid implying score calibration across unrelated queries.

concepts.title: Cross-validation folds
concepts.meaning: Held-out folds rotate so each partition measures generalization while the others train the model.
concepts.brief: Draw aligned data folds and rotate the held-out fold while training uses the remaining partitions.
pitfalls: Each example belongs to one fold per split; the held-out fold changes across rounds.

concepts.title: CUDA grid block warps
concepts.meaning: A grid contains thread blocks, each divided into groups of execution lanes.
concepts.brief: Move a tensor batch from host to device and map work into a grid of blocks and thread warps. Keep launch overhead and data placement visible for small jobs.
pitfalls: The launch grid describes program work; it does not pin a block to one SM.
Device availability and tensor placement are separate checks.

concepts.title: Data lineage
concepts.meaning: Directed record linking sources, transformations, versions, owners, and artifacts.
concepts.brief: Graph source to transform to dataset to run/checkpoint to evaluation.
pitfalls: Lineage does not prove correctness or license.

concepts.title: Training-data mixture
concepts.meaning: A training mixture assigns sampling weights to datasets before examples enter the training stream.
concepts.brief: Show source datasets contributing at different rates to one sampled training stream; expose weights as proportions.
pitfalls: Mixture weights are not the same as raw dataset sizes.

concepts.title: Data structure choices
concepts.meaning: A sequential list, indexed table, and priority tree represent different access patterns.

concepts.title: Dataset lineage gates
concepts.meaning: A source record passes through schema, identity, and group checks before a versioned dataset is released.
concepts.brief: Animate support records through schema and label checks, exact normalized fingerprints, conflict quarantine, group-level splits, near-duplicate candidate review, benchmark checks, privacy decisions, and a manifest. Keep exact identity distinct from semantic similarity; make open reviews and digest trust boundaries visible.
pitfalls: Do not treat exact hashes as semantic similarity or digest consistency as publisher authentication.
Do not split related conversation or incident records across held-out partitions.
LSH returns probabilistic candidates; keep its assumptions and review policy visible.
A scan result covers only its declared patterns and source snapshot.

concepts.title: Dataset split
concepts.meaning: Policy assigning examples to train, validation, and untouched test roles.
concepts.brief: Branch stable example IDs into split roles; tuning never touches final test.
pitfalls: Group/time/source leakage invalidates random splits.

sourceRefs.title: GLM-5.3 Training Masterclass
headings: Deduplicate before splitting, then test contamination again

concepts.title: Decision-tree split
concepts.meaning: Partitions feature space through sequential tests and assigns a prediction to each leaf.
concepts.brief: Use a tiny two-feature plane with one threshold boundary, then grow a second split and color leaves by class mix; optionally display weighted Gini or entropy reduction at the chosen split.
pitfalls: A tree split is an axis-aligned partition in the shown feature coordinates.
Impurity reduction is a training criterion, not held-out performance.

concepts.title: Denoiser
concepts.meaning: A neural network that predicts how to remove noise at a given step.

concepts.title: Diffusion
concepts.meaning: A sequence of denoising steps that turns noise into an image in pixel or latent space.

concepts.title: Distributed collective operations
concepts.meaning: Coordinates tensor movement or reduction across participating ranks.
concepts.brief: Draw ranks as lanes and animate all-reduce, reduce-scatter, all-gather, and all-to-all over a labeled ring or mesh; show payload and synchronization boundary.
pitfalls: Rank order, topology, and collective implementation affect cost and correctness.
Do not depict collectives as free shared-memory operations.

concepts.title: Distributed object reference
concepts.meaning: A future-like handle connects a remote task result to a consumer while ownership and stored bytes have separate lifetimes.
concepts.brief: Submit several remote feature tasks and keep their ObjectRef handles at the driver. Pass top-level references directly to an actor consumer so the driver need not fetch each payload; reveal local object-store copies, reference counting, owner and reconstructable task lineage as separate layers. Contrast this with serial ray.get submission and an unbounded gather.
pitfalls: An ObjectRef is a handle and dependency, not a location or a guarantee that bytes are resident on one node.
Reference metadata and retained objects still consume resources.
Task-result lineage, actor process state and durable checkpointing are different recovery contracts.

sourceRefs.title: Deep Dive - Ray
headings: Three pieces of a running job

concepts.title: Docker image layers
concepts.meaning: An image assembles reusable base and application layers into a runnable container.

concepts.title: Document chunk
concepts.meaning: A retrieval unit that keeps searchable text attached to its source location and parent structure.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Draw a page with three text bands, highlight one intact band with a bracket, and connect it to a small parent-section tab and page locator. Keep source identity visible in the silhouette. The highlight should feel like a selected passage, not a page crop.
pitfalls: Do not imply every chunk has equal meaning or length.
Do not show the selected band detached from its source and parent.
Avoid a generic file glyph with no retrieval boundary.

sourceRefs.title: Chunking Strategies
headings: What a useful chunk must preserve

concepts.title: Document evidence answer
concepts.meaning: An approved passage supports an answer through a bound, auditable evidence receipt.

concepts.title: Document page
concepts.meaning: A source page whose extracted text keeps its locator and provenance.
concepts.brief: Carry the rollback rule from a PDF page through native extraction or OCR review into a locatable record. Show why 15 becoming 1S must pause for review, preserve table row and unit structure, and carry source identity through chunking.
pitfalls: Treating a long OCR extract as proof that a critical value was recognized correctly
Detaching a number from its table row, unit, condition, or qualifier
Dropping source locators during chunking
Treating a checksum as proof of source authenticity or extraction fidelity

concepts.title: Document segmentation
concepts.meaning: A structured document becomes overlapping and section-aligned retrieval chunks.
concepts.brief: Compare fixed token windows, recursive separators, and structure-aware parent-child chunks. Measure answer completeness and citation spans at actual split boundaries.
pitfalls: Overlap repeats boundary text but cannot recover a missing condition.
Judge chunk boundaries against answerability and citation needs.

sourceRefs.title: Chunking Strategies
headings: Fixed windows show the boundary failure

concepts.title: Clipped private gradient
concepts.meaning: Per-example gradient contributions are bounded before aggregation and calibrated Gaussian noise is added.
concepts.brief: Use two-dimensional record gradients with a visible L2 clip circle. Shorten outliers to the boundary, sum the clipped vectors, animate a Gaussian perturbation, then connect sampling rate, noise multiplier, step count, adjacency, and delta to an accountant.
pitfalls: Per-batch-average clipping does not imply the same sensitivity bound as per-record clipping.
One realized noisy update does not establish a DP guarantee.
Epsilon depends on the protected unit, adjacency, sampler, noise, and all composed releases.

concepts.title: Model drift and delayed labels
concepts.meaning: Separates input distribution changes from performance evidence that arrives after outcomes mature.
concepts.brief: Plot reference and live feature distributions with a separate timeline for predictions, label maturity, and score updates; distinguish data drift alerts from measured model error.
pitfalls: Input drift alone does not establish quality degradation.
Missing labels can be delayed, selectively observed, or unavailable.

concepts.title: Edge model specialization
concepts.meaning: A compact model on a local device is tuned to one focused task.

concepts.title: Embedding
concepts.meaning: A learned vector that places an item in a space of relationships.

concepts.title: Embedding metric geometry
concepts.meaning: Vector angle and length make different similarity measures visible.
concepts.brief: Show query and candidate vectors. Recompute dot product, cosine similarity, and Euclidean distance, then apply a declared normalization and quantization contract.
pitfalls: Cosine ignores positive magnitude while dot product can depend on it.
Normalization is an explicit serving contract.

concepts.title: Embedding neighborhood map
concepts.meaning: Shows how a similarity metric ranks nearby vectors in a learned representation space.
concepts.brief: Draw a labeled point cloud with a query vector, cosine-angle and Euclidean-distance rulers, nearest-neighbor highlights, and an optional PCA projection toggle; retain vector labels and metric readouts.
pitfalls: A two-dimensional projection can distort global distances and hide task-relevant dimensions.
Equal vector dimensions do not prove compatible coordinate systems.

concepts.title: Estimation interval
concepts.meaning: Repeated sample estimates gather around a central estimate inside an uncertainty interval.

concepts.title: Evaluation slices
concepts.meaning: A suite-level score and per-slice results expose a safety failure hidden by an aggregate.

concepts.title: Evaluation gate
concepts.meaning: A versioned pass/fail checkpoint that combines policy constraints, quality evidence, and release ownership before exposure expands.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Show frozen cases entering distinct rows for hard policy checks, quality metrics, and slice checks. Each row emits a labeled receipt into a final gate, where a failed hard requirement visibly blocks promotion even if aggregate quality is high.
pitfalls: Hard safety and authorization constraints cannot be averaged away.
A metric does not validate the dataset or evaluator by itself.
The gate should identify its version, threshold, owner, and failure path.

concepts.title: Evaluation row
concepts.meaning: One replayable graded case joining fixed inputs, observed behavior, grader evidence, and version pins.
concepts.brief: Receipt tile for fixture, output, grader, latency, and model pins; show one row separate from aggregate.
pitfalls: An aggregate is not a dataset snapshot.

sourceRefs.title: AI Engineer Portfolio Projects for Interviews

concepts.title: Evidence packet
concepts.meaning: A compact, ordered set of retrieved passages with enough source, version, permission, and location data to support a response.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Stack two to four slim passage cards. Each has a source dot, a short highlighted phrase, and a tiny version/location tab; one larger parent card behind them shows context packing. Leave one empty slot or visible gap to signal that the maximum pack size may be underfilled.
pitfalls: Ranking is not support; the generator still needs claim-level verification.
Do not erase source IDs or versions when packing context.
A maximum token budget does not require filling every slot.

sourceRefs.title: Production RAG Pipelines
headings: Pack evidence for a grounded answer

concepts.title: Evidence retrieval pipeline
concepts.meaning: Versioned source evidence passes access filtering and ranking before it supports an answer.
concepts.brief: Attach source identity, version, and location to chunks. Filter by caller permissions before ranking, pack cited evidence, and abstain when passages do not resolve the answer.
pitfalls: Authorization must run before evidence reaches generation.
A citation points to a span; it does not prove the span supports the claim.

sourceRefs.title: Production RAG Pipelines
headings: Pack evidence for a grounded answer

concepts.title: Expert
concepts.meaning: A feed-forward network inside a routed transformer layer.

concepts.title: Fairness matched pairs
concepts.meaning: Equivalent cases travel in parallel while one controlled attribute changes.
concepts.brief: Construct matched examples with one declared wording or identity change. Compare scores, decisions, and subgroup errors under the same task contract and data snapshot.
pitfalls: A matched-pair test supports a narrow behavioral comparison, not a universal fairness claim.
Preserve decision-relevant facts while changing the audited feature.

concepts.title: Fallback route
concepts.meaning: Policy-controlled alternate destination used when preferred route is unavailable or ineligible.
concepts.brief: Primary/fallback lanes expose health, privacy, and cost decisions.
pitfalls: Fallback changes model, privacy, latency, and cost.

sourceRefs.title: Best AI Plans for OpenClaw in 2026
headings: Make paid fallback an explicit decision

concepts.title: Feature centering
concepts.meaning: Per-token normalization centers and rescales feature coordinates before learned affine adjustments.
concepts.brief: Animate mean subtraction and variance scaling, then compare residual and gradient paths around normalization.
pitfalls: Keep reduction axes explicit, preserve epsilon, and avoid interpreting an identity path as a lower bound on the full gradient.

concepts.title: Feature contract vector
concepts.meaning: Named measurements pass through type and availability checks into fixed ordered model coordinates.
concepts.brief: Build the 09:00 J-204 prediction row from event and availability clocks, then show fitted numeric transforms, missingness indicators, categorical encoding, a fixed feature order, a preprocessing edit, and offline/serving parity. Keep illustrative coefficients and thresholds labeled as authored examples.
pitfalls: Exclude future events and labels even when present in today's backfill.
Robust scaling does not clip outliers.
Smoothing does not replace out-of-fold or time-aware target encoding.
Preprocessing changes affect only inputs they actually alter; measure the paired model behavior.

concepts.title: FlashAttention tile dataflow
concepts.meaning: FlashAttention reuses query, key, and value tiles in fast memory to reduce high-bandwidth memory traffic.
concepts.brief: Move compact query, key, and value tiles through on-chip memory while updating output state without writing a full attention matrix.
pitfalls: Memory traffic and score-matrix materialization are the focus.

concepts.title: Floating-point formats
concepts.meaning: Represents signed values with finite exponent range and finite precision determined by a bit layout.
concepts.brief: Design a scalable bit-field SVG for sign, exponent, and fraction; pair it with neighboring representable numbers and range/precision comparisons for FP16, BF16, FP32, and FP8 variants.
pitfalls: Range and precision are different properties.
Label the exact format and bias; bit allocations vary.

concepts.title: Forecast and alert
concepts.meaning: A frozen forecast is compared with mature outcomes before an operational alert fires.

concepts.title: Forecast residual band
concepts.meaning: A forecast center and uncertainty band are compared with observed values and their residuals.
concepts.brief: Animate a timestamped demand fixture across a rolling forecast origin, update the baseline and forecast interval, reveal residuals only after observations arrive, and compare anomaly thresholds with normal seasonal variation. Label authored values as illustrative and preserve future-data boundaries.
pitfalls: Forecasts use information available at their origin; later observations belong to scoring the forecast.
Residual alarms require seasonality, horizon, and uncertainty context.
Prediction intervals express uncertainty under a model and data regime; they are not guaranteed bounds.
Keep illustrative fixtures distinct from measured forecast performance.

concepts.title: Sharded training state
concepts.meaning: Parameters, gradients, and optimizer states are partitioned across training devices and gathered as computation needs them.
concepts.brief: Start with replicated weight, gradient, and optimizer slots on four training ranks. Reveal ZeRO stages as successive shards; animate FSDP parameter all-gather before a wrapped unit and gradient reduce-scatter after backward.
pitfalls: The ledger excludes activation memory and temporary communication buffers unless shown.
Full sharding trades memory for collectives and depends on unit wrapping and topology.
Training-state sharding differs from inference tensor parallelism.

concepts.title: Tiled matrix multiplication
concepts.meaning: Reuses input tiles in fast local memory to reduce global-memory traffic during matrix multiplication.
concepts.brief: Animate small A and B tiles loaded from global memory into shared SRAM, multiply-accumulate into a register tile, then write output. Expose tile reuse, edge predicates, and accumulator precision.
pitfalls: Tile shapes and supported arithmetic depend on hardware and kernel contracts.
Reduced-precision products may still use higher-precision accumulation.

sourceRefs.title: GEMM From Naive CUDA to Tensor Cores

concepts.title: Generalization curve
concepts.meaning: Training error falls with capacity while held-out error can rise as a model fits sample-specific noise.

concepts.title: Git history bisect
concepts.meaning: Commit snapshots narrow a regression to the change that introduced it.

concepts.title: GPT training loop
concepts.meaning: A causal decoder predicts the next token, updates weights from loss and samples from the checkpoint.
concepts.brief: Pack a contiguous token stream into context windows and shifted next-token labels. Reveal causal attention, loss and weight update, then sample from the resulting checkpoint and resume from saved optimizer state.
pitfalls: Input tokens and next-token labels are shifted by one position.
Held-out chunks must not be concatenated into fake transitions.

sourceRefs.title: Build GPT from Scratch Lab
headings: What a resume file has to remember

concepts.title: GPU
concepts.meaning: A processor built to run many numerical operations in parallel.

sourceRefs.title: Run Gemma 4 with Ollama: Model Tags and Memory Requirements
Run Qwen3.6 Locally with llama.cpp and Unsloth GGUF

concepts.title: GPU autoscale pool
concepts.meaning: Queue pressure triggers new GPU replicas that become ready after warmup.
concepts.brief: Track arrivals, queue age, warm replicas, cold-start time, and capacity at each control interval. Scale before the service target is breached and verify replicas before routing traffic.
pitfalls: GPU utilization alone may hide queue growth and latency.
A scheduled replica serves no traffic until its model is loaded and warmed.

sourceRefs.title: GPU Serving & Autoscaling
headings: A burst needs capacity before its deadline

concepts.title: GPU execution hierarchy
concepts.meaning: Maps host launches and memory ownership to GPU grids, blocks, threads, warps, and multiprocessors.
concepts.brief: Show a CPU host launching a grid of blocks; expand one block into warps/threads mapped onto an SM, with separate host and device-memory regions and synchronization points.
pitfalls: Terminology and scheduling details vary by accelerator and architecture.
Use separate counts for logical threads and physical execution lanes.

concepts.title: GPU memory ledger
concepts.meaning: Accounting of weights, activations, optimizer, cache, workspaces, and reserve.
concepts.brief: Stack budget responds to batch/context/concurrency; separate training and inference.
pitfalls: Model file size is not total memory use.

sourceRefs.title: Run Gemma 4 with Ollama: Model Tags and Memory Requirements

concepts.title: GPU timing boundary
concepts.meaning: Host submission and asynchronous device work require a declared scope and synchronization boundary.

concepts.title: Warm GPU capacity
concepts.meaning: The staged path from scheduled hardware through model load and warmup to replicas that can safely receive traffic.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Three GPU tiles move from pending node to loading checkpoint to warm ready state. The traffic arrow reaches only the ready tile. Show a small timer near cold-start loading, not a generic speed flame.
pitfalls: Scheduled does not mean loaded; loaded does not necessarily mean healthy.
A warm pool consumes cost and memory before traffic arrives.
Do not equate GPU utilization with capacity readiness.

concepts.title: Gradient
concepts.meaning: A direction and rate of change that guide parameter updates.

concepts.title: Gradient descent landscape
concepts.meaning: Shows how a parameter update follows a local gradient on an objective surface.
concepts.brief: Render a 2D contour surface over two parameters with a live point, gradient arrow, and short sequence of proposed updates; allow learning-rate changes to reveal stable, slow, and overshooting paths.
pitfalls: Convex bowls are teaching examples; many neural-network objectives are nonconvex.
The gradient arrow is local and depends on the displayed coordinates and scale.

concepts.title: Graph evidence path
concepts.meaning: A multi-hop chain through source-linked entities and relationships that supplies a broader evidence set for a query.
concepts.brief: 16:9 diagram. Draw two or three named entity nodes joined by different, explicitly labeled relations. Each edge carries a small source locator. Animate traversal from question to first entity, across a supported relation, then back to the passages that support the path. Distinguish asserted relationship from causal explanation.
pitfalls: An extracted edge is an investigation lead unless its source supports the relationship.
Entity resolution may be uncertain and tenant or environment scoped.
Graph traversal and learned message passing are different operations.

concepts.title: Grouped GEMM padding and scale
concepts.meaning: Uneven expert token groups pack into an aligned M axis whose padding trades useful work for scheduling efficiency.
concepts.brief: Route tokens into four expert groups with 64, 192, 32 and 128 valid rows. Pack each segment to a declared M alignment, show the concatenated launch grid, highlight useful versus padded rows, and unpack outputs back to original token order. Compare one persistent grouped launch with separate per-expert launches while measuring total time and useful-token throughput.
pitfalls: M counts token-expert assignments, not unique source tokens.
Padding can raise traffic and arithmetic work; a single launch can still win if it amortizes launch cost.
Configured and theoretical alignment helpers may differ on a pinned hardware/library snapshot.

concepts.title: Grouped query head map
concepts.meaning: Several query heads connect to fewer shared key and value heads.
concepts.brief: Keep all query heads visible while grouping them onto fewer K/V heads. Count cache heads and compare MHA, GQA, and MQA at a fixed head dimension.
pitfalls: GQA reduces K/V heads; it does not remove query heads.
Changing K/V sharing changes the model function and may require uptraining.

concepts.title: GUI observe act loop
concepts.meaning: A screen observation grounds a click, then the updated screen confirms the result.
concepts.brief: Alternate observation, target grounding, host authorization, action dispatch, and new-state verification. Keep the agent proposal distinct from the host decision.
pitfalls: A screenshot or accessibility label can be stale or ambiguous.
A typed schema does not guarantee correct target grounding.

concepts.title: HNSW graph search
concepts.meaning: Approximate nearest-neighbor search that navigates a layered proximity graph and retains a bounded candidate set.
concepts.brief: 16:9 simulation on a fixed, labeled point cloud. Begin at an upper-layer entry node, move through a few long-range links toward the query, descend while retaining the same vector identity, then expand several neighbors in the base layer. Keep visited, retained, and unvisited nodes visually distinct. Offer an adjustable search-width control.
pitfalls: The returned set is not a certificate of exact nearest neighbors.
Graph edges are navigation links, not semantic relations or proof of relevance.
Do not confuse retained-result width with number of layers.

concepts.title: Human review queue
concepts.meaning: A work queue that presents bounded, attributable decisions to reviewers while preserving hard policy gates and escalation rules.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Stack review cards by risk and deadline with one selected packet expanded to show the exact action, cited evidence, and decision controls. Keep a separate route for hard-deny cases so queue triage cannot lower the safety floor.
pitfalls: A reviewer cannot approve an action without seeing the exact action and evidence.
Queue priority is not permission to skip policy.
Model summaries and untrusted content need clear visual separation.

sourceRefs.title: Data Labeling and Human Feedback
headings: Write the rubric before collecting preferences
Select cases that might teach something new

concepts.title: Hybrid search lanes
concepts.meaning: Parallel lexical and dense retrieval paths whose ranked candidates are fused into one eligible result set.
concepts.brief: 16:9 vector diagram. Start with one query and one shared authorization/freshness gate, then split into a lexical lane that lights up exact identifiers and a dense lane that matches paraphrases. Show each lane producing a ranked list, then fuse by rank with reciprocal-rank fusion and pass candidates onward. Animate the same stale or forbidden document staying outside both lanes.
pitfalls: Apply the same hard filters to every lane before fusion.
Do not add incomparable raw score values as if they had the same calibration.
Fusion can still rank an irrelevant candidate first.

concepts.title: Idempotency fence
concepts.meaning: Stable key or lease token preventing duplicate effects from retries or stale workers.
concepts.brief: Duplicate attempts share key; stale lease rejected at write boundary.
pitfalls: Requires atomic state and downstream deduplication.

concepts.title: Image text alignment
concepts.meaning: Image and text representations meet in a shared similarity space.

concepts.title: Inference latency clocks
concepts.meaning: A long initial processing segment is followed by repeated token intervals.
concepts.brief: Place request, first-token, and later-token timestamps on a timeline. Compute TTFT and inter-token latency, then separate queue, prefill, and decode segments.
pitfalls: Define metric start and end events before reporting.
End-to-end output rate includes initial wait and differs from decode cadence.

concepts.title: Instruction boundary
concepts.meaning: A model application distinguishes trusted instructions from untrusted evidence while enforcing authority in code.
concepts.brief: Follow an evaluation report that contains a factual result and an injected deployment command. Keep source labels visible, let the model propose text or a typed action, then show the application checking identity, capability, arguments, and approval before any protected sink.
pitfalls: Treating XML tags, role labels, or repeated reminders as a security boundary
Describing prompt injection as a text pattern that a perfect classifier can remove
Assuming the injected command has authority because the application fetched its source
Confusing a helpful refusal with a blocked unauthorized side effect

concepts.title: Causal intervention
concepts.meaning: An intervention sets a treatment value and removes its usual incoming causes from the causal graph.
concepts.brief: Contrast an observed incoming causal edge with a direct intervention marker on treatment, then preserve downstream effects.
pitfalls: Separate intervention from conditioning on an observed value.

concepts.title: Inverted index
concepts.meaning: Term keys connect to ordered posting-list entries for matching documents.
concepts.brief: Connect term entries to ordered posting lists. Show term frequency or position metadata separately from document identifiers, then score candidates with a lexical ranking rule.
pitfalls: An inverted index maps terms to candidate documents; it does not rank semantic relevance by itself.
Posting lists may store frequencies and positions in addition to identifiers.

sourceRefs.title: Hybrid Search, BM25 & Reranking
headings: Sparse retrieval starts with an inverted index

concepts.title: IVF centroid probing
concepts.meaning: An approximate search that assigns vectors to centroid lists and scans only a chosen number of nearest lists.
concepts.brief: 16:9 simulation. Show a 2D embedding field partitioned into Voronoi-like cells with one centroid per cell. Place a query, rank the centroids, illuminate the nearest nprobe cells, and scan their posting-list dots. Keep a relevant vector in an unprobed cell so increasing nprobe visibly recovers it at additional work.
pitfalls: nlist counts stored partitions; nprobe counts searched lists.
A cell boundary is an index partition, not a semantic category.
Do not imply every true neighbor lies in a probed list.

sourceRefs.title: Vector DB Internals: HNSW & IVF
headings: A boundary miss: `nprobe = 1` drops a true neighbor

concepts.title: JAX transform pipeline
concepts.meaning: JAX wraps a pure function with gradient, batching and compilation transformations over pytree state.
concepts.brief: Start with a pure scalar loss over structured parameter leaves. Derive gradients, batch the function with vmap, and compile a shape-specific call with jit, making each transformation visible as a callable wrapper.
pitfalls: Transformations derive callable functions; they are not sequential runtime lifecycle stages.
JIT specialization depends on compatible shapes and static control flow.

sourceRefs.title: JAX for PyTorch Researchers
headings: Transform one small function at a time
Transformation order changes the derived program

concepts.title: Option pointer decision
concepts.meaning: A decision readout scores the options that were actually offered and can preserve an abstain route.

concepts.title: Judge agreement
concepts.meaning: Agreement between automated evaluators and human labels under one rubric.
concepts.brief: Two rubric cards grade identical cases; reveal discordant examples.
pitfalls: Agreement is consistency, not truth.

concepts.title: Judge rubric
concepts.meaning: Two candidate answers are evaluated against the same explicit criteria and reviewed labels.
concepts.brief: Show an explicit pairwise rubric, swap A/B order while keeping candidate text fixed, compare blinded human judgments, and compute disagreement, coverage, and agreement on an illustrative labeled fixture. Separate bias probes from validity and report the reviewed denominator.
pitfalls: Treating a judge score as independent proof of answer quality
Calling order sensitivity a universal fixed preference direction
Reporting agreement without the eligible reviewed denominator
Using accuracy alone when class imbalance or abstentions matter

concepts.title: Kernel candidate gates
concepts.meaning: A candidate earns a performance claim only after correctness, safety, comparable timing and traffic checks.

concepts.title: Kernel fusion traffic
concepts.meaning: Fusion keeps intermediate values local so adjacent operations avoid writing and rereading temporary tensors.

concepts.title: Inspector-executor plan contract
concepts.meaning: A metadata plan assigns irregular requests to GPU tiles and workspace that a stable attention run consumes.
concepts.brief: Show three requests with different query lengths and scattered KV pages. A CPU-side inspector reads offsets and page metadata once, assigns tiles, sizes scratch workspace and decides whether to split KV work. The executor consumes the plan plus query/cache tensors, emits partial states when needed, then merges them. Animate compatibility checks for lengths, masks, pointer layout and workspace lifetime; distinguish a reusable plan from stale decode metadata.
pitfalls: A plan is reusable only across compatible batch specifications; decode lengths can change between steps.
Stable buffer addresses do not make stale metadata contents correct.
The pinned prefill plan performs host-side work and copies, so verify graph-capture constraints for the selected wrapper.

sourceRefs.title: Deep Dive - FlashInfer
headings: Plan then run: inspector-executor for GPU kernels

concepts.title: Kernel tiling
concepts.meaning: Processing large tensors in bounded tiles with near-compute staging and reuse.
concepts.brief: Tiles move through memory hierarchy, compute, and accumulate.
pitfalls: Tile shapes are hardware-specific; merge math must stay valid.

concepts.title: Key
concepts.meaning: A vector that describes what information a token offers.

concepts.title: KV capacity budget
concepts.meaning: Weights and working memory leave a limited region for active key and value state.

concepts.title: KV cache handoff
concepts.meaning: A serving system transfers prompt-derived key and value state to the worker that will generate tokens.
concepts.brief: Trace one request's ownership and KV blocks from prefill to decode. Compute payload bytes from token, layer, head, and dtype dimensions; reserve destination capacity before transfer, validate matching model/layout metadata, and separate transport completion from request execution and client delivery.
pitfalls: Treating a transfer engine as the owner of a request or its retry policy
Assuming all state layouts or worker versions are interchangeable
Counting enqueue as transfer completion or transfer completion as a generated response
Retrying an uncertain transfer or downstream action without an operation identity and reconciliation

concepts.title: Latency and service metrics
concepts.meaning: Measurements separating first-token time, inter-token delay, throughput, and useful work.
concepts.brief: Timeline and fleet chart distinguish TTFT/ITL/TPOT/TPS/goodput.
pitfalls: Metrics use different denominators and windows.

sourceRefs.title: 50 LLM Interview Questions for 2026
headings: 11. Fleet TPS rose and users still wait. How do TTFT, ITL, TPOT, and TPS differ?

concepts.title: Request latency waterfall
concepts.meaning: A timeline that places each request stage on one declared clock and distinguishes serial work from overlapped work.
concepts.brief: 16:9 timeline with identity, admission, retrieval, prefill, first token, decode, and response completion. Mark the TTFT stop point and end-to-end stop point. Support parallel lanes so retrieval and independent tool reads visibly overlap; use a second inset for inter-token gaps.
pitfalls: State the start and stop events for every metric.
Do not add component p95 values as if their sum were request p95.
Inter-token gaps, TPOT, TTFT, and total latency answer different questions.

headings: Scheduled, started, and ready are different states
