headings: Trace the request before estimating a percentile
Tail latency hazards and fan-out variance
Latency waterfall economics and deployment gates

sourceRefs.title: Real-Time Voice AI Agent
headings: The latency budget: a worked example

concepts.title: Latent posterior cloud
concepts.meaning: An encoder describes a distribution of possible latent codes for an observed input.
concepts.brief: Transform an independent noise point into a posterior sample and decode it.
pitfalls: Distinguish posterior from prior, standard deviation from variance, and reconstruction from sampling quality.

concepts.title: Latent responsibilities
concepts.meaning: Expectation-maximization assigns each observation fractional membership in mixture components.

concepts.title: Learning-rate schedule
concepts.meaning: Changes the optimizer step scale according to training progress.
concepts.brief: Draw a timeline with warmup followed by selectable constant, linear-decay, and cosine-decay curves; pair the curve with current step and scalar learning rate.
pitfalls: The schedule changes update scale, not the gradient direction.
Avoid implying one schedule is universally best.

concepts.title: LLM API request
concepts.meaning: An authenticated server turns a user task into a bounded provider request and records the result.
concepts.brief: Route a browser task through backend authentication, tenant authorization, trusted database facts, redaction and a typed provider request. Return a traceable result and show a retry reusing its idempotency key.
pitfalls: Provider credentials stay on the server and outside client bundles.
A timeout leaves the remote outcome uncertain; use idempotency and reconcile before repeating side effects.

sourceRefs.title: Calling LLM APIs in Production
headings: A task contract for the model

concepts.title: LLM lifecycle
concepts.meaning: A model moves from pre-training through post-training, evaluation, compression and deployment.

concepts.title: Local model memory map
concepts.meaning: Model weights and active state occupy separate device and host memory pools.
concepts.brief: Budget weights, K/V state, workspace, and reserve across GPU, unified, and host memory. Show how block offload changes where execution occurs.
pitfalls: CPU offload can change latency and throughput substantially.
Model size alone omits cache, workspace, and allocator overhead.

sourceRefs.title: Local & Edge LLM Deployment
headings: Build a budget for each memory pool

concepts.title: LoRA
concepts.meaning: Low-rank factors that add a trainable update to frozen weights.

concepts.title: Loss
concepts.meaning: A score that measures how far a model prediction is from its target.

concepts.title: Dynamic loss scaling controller
concepts.meaning: Scales a training loss to keep small gradients representable, then detects overflow before the optimizer update.
concepts.brief: Trace scale-up before backward, gradient unscale before clipping, finite-value check, optimizer-step skip on overflow, and scale backoff/growth across iterations.
pitfalls: Loss scaling changes numerical range during gradient computation; it does not improve model quality by itself.
Keep unscale and finite checks before the optimizer step.

concepts.title: Matrix
concepts.meaning: A rectangular array of numbers transformed by model layers.

concepts.title: Memory retention valve
concepts.meaning: Gates control how stored recurrent evidence survives and how a candidate enters the state.
concepts.brief: Follow an old-state amount through retention, addition, and exposure.
pitfalls: Keep cell and hidden state distinct, identify gate convention, and isolate the direct gradient path.

sourceRefs.title: RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and Sequence Modeling

concepts.title: ML release tuple
concepts.meaning: A release binds data, features, model, policy, monitor and rollback artifact before promotion.

concepts.title: Model
concepts.meaning: A learned network that maps input signals to useful outputs.

concepts.title: Model weight merge
concepts.meaning: Compatible model parameter tensors contribute to one merged checkpoint that must be evaluated.
concepts.brief: Display matching tensors from models fine-tuned from the same base, calculate a weighted midpoint, and trace held-out loss along the interpolation path. Contrast with a one-dimensional double-well example where averaging across separated minima raises loss.
pitfalls: Parameter names and tensor shapes do not prove neuron alignment.
Averaging unrelated independently initialized checkpoints can fail.
Evaluate real merged checkpoints on held-out tasks after checking the toy interpolation.

concepts.title: Model monitoring drift
concepts.meaning: Reference and current feature distributions are compared as a monitored shift is surfaced for review.
concepts.brief: Follow a deployed model from stable feature distributions through an input shift, delayed labels, outcome metrics, and a canary decision. Separate feature drift, prediction drift, data quality, and delayed outcome evidence; compare to a fixed reference and show uncertainty before rollback decisions.
pitfalls: Feature drift is a review signal, not proof of model degradation.
Without labels, outcome quality may be delayed or unavailable.
A single aggregate metric can hide segment failures and changing traffic mix.
Rollback or retraining thresholds need explicit operational evidence and ownership.

concepts.title: Model parallelism topologies
concepts.meaning: Splits model computation or state across devices along different dimensions.
concepts.brief: Show the same transformer mapped as replicated data-parallel workers, tensor-parallel shards within a layer, pipeline stages across layers, context shards, and expert ownership. Use separate colors for communication edges.
pitfalls: Parallelism modes shard different axes and introduce distinct communication patterns.
A combined topology has divisibility and placement constraints.

concepts.title: Model routing constraints
concepts.meaning: A request passes hard policy checks before reaching eligible model lanes.

concepts.title: Mixture of experts
concepts.meaning: A router sends each token through a selected subset of expert networks.

concepts.title: Apple unified memory
concepts.meaning: CPU and GPU share physical system memory while a device change can still create a distinct buffer.

concepts.title: Multimodal fusion bridge
concepts.meaning: Image, sound, and text signals enter a shared representation path.
concepts.brief: Follow modality encoders into prefix tokens, side memory, or late fusion while preserving source timestamps and image regions along the shared answer path.
pitfalls: Fusion strategies meet at different model stages.
A pooled similarity vector cannot replace spatial grounding or timestamp evidence.

sourceRefs.title: Vision-Language & Multimodal Architectures
headings: The concept: one shared evidence path

concepts.title: Neuron signal
concepts.meaning: A neuron combines weighted inputs, applies an activation function, and sends an output signal.
concepts.brief: Route input signals into a neuron, then show its activated output as one outgoing signal.
pitfalls: Keep weighted input, activation, and output stages distinct.

concepts.title: Next-token logits
concepts.meaning: Logits score candidate next tokens before softmax converts them into probabilities.
concepts.brief: Show signed candidate scores from the final hidden state and highlight the largest logit before probability normalization.
pitfalls: Keep logits distinct from normalized probabilities.

concepts.title: Noise
concepts.meaning: A random signal mixed into data during diffusion training or generation.

concepts.title: Online softmax
concepts.meaning: Online softmax updates a running maximum and normalizer as attention scores arrive tile by tile.
concepts.brief: Stream score tiles into a running maximum and rescaled normalizer so the full score matrix need not be stored.
pitfalls: Show rescaling of earlier contributions when the running maximum changes.

concepts.title: Optimizer state and moments
concepts.meaning: Maintains gradient history and coordinate scale to compute parameter updates.
concepts.brief: Show a parameter beside its gradient stream, momentum buffer m, squared-gradient buffer v, bias-corrected values, and the resulting update. Add a separate decoupled weight-decay arrow for AdamW.
pitfalls: Adam second moment averages squared gradients and is not statistical variance.
Keep weight decay distinct from the adaptive-gradient term.

concepts.title: Optimizer trajectory
concepts.meaning: Momentum combines a gradient with running velocity that carries updates through a curved loss surface.
concepts.brief: Trace an optimizer through elongated loss contours; compare direct gradient steps with a momentum path toward a minimum.
pitfalls: Keep contour geometry and trajectory direction consistent with descent.

concepts.title: Paired outcomes
concepts.meaning: Two systems are evaluated on matched tasks so ties and directional changes remain visible.
concepts.brief: Keep each prompt, both model outcomes, and the shared hidden tests in one row. Show five ties and one B-only win, then condition on disagreement count and animate fair-coin outcomes under the null. Compare the exact one-sided tail for one of one and thirteen of sixteen wins. Continue to false-positive and missed-improvement decisions, the search cost of twenty comparisons, paired-row bootstrap lift, and a separate pass-at-k candidate budget.
pitfalls: A p-value is a tail probability under the null, not the probability that the null is true.
Ties contribute to pass rates and lift but not the conditional sign-test win count.
The test direction and comparison family must be declared before looking at results.
Bootstrap resample frequency is not a null p-value.
Prompt variants and repeated tasks can violate independent-task assumptions.

sourceRefs.title: AI Lab Technical Presentation
headings: Inspect the cases behind the average

concepts.title: Patch to token
concepts.meaning: A spatial pixel patch becomes a projected vector while its location remains separately represented.
concepts.brief: Follow raster-order patch values through a shared projection and position-aware attention, then count visual slots.
pitfalls: Keep patch count, raw width, hidden width, and bridge output count separate. Evaluate exact detail after preprocessing.

concepts.title: Permission filter
concepts.meaning: Policy check limiting retrieved candidates to caller-authorized scope.
concepts.brief: Identity/query enters ACL filter; denied docs stop before packing.
pitfalls: Filtering after generation is too late.

sourceRefs.title: Context Engineering: Beyond Prompting
headings: Retrieval is also a permission boundary

concepts.title: Persistent memory tiers
concepts.meaning: Working context can write to and recall from several durable memory layers.
concepts.brief: Separate current working context from durable sourced memories. Retrieve by relevance and recency, preserve provenance and permissions, and write only useful records with explicit retention.
pitfalls: Agent memory is application-managed state, not the model KV cache.
A stored memory may be stale, unauthorized, or unsupported when recalled.

concepts.title: Position
concepts.meaning: An item's location in an ordered token sequence.

concepts.title: Precision scale accumulate
concepts.meaning: Compact operands receive scaling before multiplication and wider-precision accumulation.
concepts.brief: Encode operands on a reduced range and precision grid, apply required scales, then accumulate products at the declared precision. Measure rounding, underflow, and saturation.
pitfalls: Scaling cannot restore values already rounded to zero or saturated.
Format bit widths do not specify an entire kernel arithmetic path.

sourceRefs.title: Low-Precision GPU Programming
headings: Format taxonomy: range, spacing, and bitfields
Scale ownership and the GEMM dataflow

concepts.title: From text to a useful prediction
concepts.meaning: An application collects input, calls a learned model, presents the prediction, and saves useful results.
concepts.brief: Follow one support message from a browser through an HTTP endpoint into a text classifier. Show the returned probability vector, the threshold that selects automatic handling or review, and the saved result. Keep model prediction separate from the routing decision.
pitfalls: A high model score needs measured calibration before it can be read as an observed success rate.
Application tests and labeled model evaluation answer different questions.

sourceRefs.title: First AI App End-to-End
headings: Turn that prediction into an API

concepts.title: Preference
concepts.meaning: A comparison that records which of two responses a person favors.

concepts.title: Preference-training pipeline
concepts.meaning: Turns comparisons between responses into a reward model or a direct preference-optimization objective.
concepts.brief: Show prompt plus chosen/rejected responses feeding a pairwise score difference, Bradley-Terry sigmoid/BCE, and reward-head update; optionally branch to PPO with a reference policy or DPO direct policy loss.
pitfalls: Human preference labels measure the annotation contract and can contain noise or bias.
Reward-model score is a learned proxy; keep held-out human evaluation visible.

concepts.title: Preference vote
concepts.meaning: A labeler's comparison identifies which of two complete answers better meets the same request.
concepts.brief: Keep the prompt fixed. Show chosen and rejected answers, compute each policy/reference log-probability ratio, subtract to obtain the DPO margin, then update the two response likelihoods with the reference anchor visible.
pitfalls: Do not imply DPO is an online reward-model loop.
DPO and PPO can produce different checkpoints; compare the resulting policies on the same evaluation.
Shared parameters can lower both absolute sequence probabilities while improving the relative margin.

concepts.title: Shared prefix block
concepts.meaning: Two prompt lanes share a complete initial block before their tokens diverge.
concepts.brief: Align prompts token by token, share only compatible full prefix blocks, and allocate private storage after divergence. Include model, adapter, position, and isolation identity.
pitfalls: Matching sentences alone is insufficient when earlier context differs.
A reused prefix saves prompt computation; continuations still read their history.

concepts.title: Prefix trie
concepts.meaning: Tree sharing common prefixes for lookup and reuse.
concepts.brief: Token branches share cached prefix, then diverge.
pitfalls: Eviction and authorization are separate policies.

sourceRefs.title: Deep Dive - SGLang
headings: RadixAttention: prefix reuse as a tree

concepts.title: Principal axis
concepts.meaning: A principal component points along a direction of greatest centered data variance.
concepts.brief: Generate a small anisotropic cloud with two visible groups, animate Lloyd assignment and centroid updates from fixed initial centers, and report inertia for the resulting partition. Then center the same points, compute covariance and a leading eigenvector, and rotate a unit-scaled coordinate frame to show projected variance and reconstruction error. Distinguish cluster labels from PCA coordinates, explain feature scaling and local optima, and note that PCA preserves variance rather than task relevance.
pitfalls: K-means minimizes within-cluster squared Euclidean distance and favors compact roughly spherical groups.
Results depend on initialization and feature scaling.
PCA centers data before computing principal directions.
Equal pixels per unit are required when the drawing represents Euclidean distances or angles.
High-variance directions need not preserve downstream predictive information.

concepts.title: Differential privacy adjacency
concepts.meaning: A visual comparison of datasets that differ by one stated protected unit and the bounded output distributions a randomized mechanism should produce.
concepts.brief: 16:9 simulation. Place two datasets side by side with one clearly identified person or conversation added or removed. Pass both through the same randomized mechanism and plot overlapping output distributions with epsilon and delta labels. Add a composition counter across multiple releases.
pitfalls: Differential privacy is not anonymization or a property of hashing names.
Show the chosen person/record/conversation adjacency convention explicitly.
Do not present toy epsilon or delta values as a recommended budget.

sourceRefs.title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
headings: Start with the unit you promise to protect

concepts.title: Probability calibration
concepts.meaning: Agreement between stated probabilities and observed frequencies.
concepts.brief: Reliability plot with bins, diagonal, sample counts, and miscalibration.
pitfalls: Calibration differs from ranking and depends on population.

concepts.title: Probability mass
concepts.meaning: A discrete distribution assigns probability mass to outcomes, with the masses summing to one.

concepts.title: Bounded agent workflow
concepts.meaning: Trusted admission, verified evidence and a bounded action precede a separately authorized write.

concepts.title: Projection distance map
concepts.meaning: Points in a plane cast onto a shorter coordinate axis with visible displacement.

concepts.title: Prompt
concepts.meaning: Instructions and context supplied to a model.

sourceRefs.title: Best AI Plans for OpenClaw in 2026
How Decision Models Like Jev Work: AI Without the Paragraph
LLM Inference Engines Compared: vLLM, SGLang, Ollama & llama.cpp
RAG vs Fine-Tuning vs Prompting: A Practical Guide

concepts.title: Prompt search loop
concepts.meaning: Prompt candidates are scored on validation examples and then checked against a separate holdout.
concepts.brief: Generate candidate instructions from training examples, score them against an explicit validation metric, and preserve a separate holdout for final evaluation.
pitfalls: An optimizer can exploit a flawed metric.
Tuning on holdout examples leaks evaluation feedback into prompt selection.

sourceRefs.title: Prompt Optimization with DSPy
headings: Search instructions as well as demonstrations

concepts.title: Provider fallback route
concepts.meaning: A route selector that first removes lanes violating hard requirements, then ranks compatible providers and revalidates fallback output.
concepts.brief: 16:9 diagram. Compile privacy, capability, deadline, and data-region constraints into an eligible set before ranking by policy. When the preferred route fails, choose the next eligible lane only if remaining time and required capabilities still fit; validate its response against the same contract.
pitfalls: A healthy backup may lack the required access to the source or capability.
A cheaper estimate is not a charge ceiling or quality guarantee.
A generation retry must not repeat a completed write.

concepts.title: Python data flow
concepts.meaning: A keyed record becomes a batch of rows whose labels feed an explicit comparison.

concepts.title: Quantization
concepts.meaning: Mapping high-precision values onto a smaller set of representable levels.

sourceRefs.title: Run Gemma 4 with Ollama: Model Tags and Memory Requirements

concepts.title: Query
concepts.meaning: A learned request vector that compares with keys to find relevant context.

concepts.title: Query expansion paths
concepts.meaning: One question becomes several focused retrieval paths whose results are combined.
concepts.brief: Create a standalone rewrite, vocabulary variants, decomposed plan, or hypothetical answer embedding from one question. Retrieve and fuse results while tracking evidence coverage.
pitfalls: HyDE embeds a generated passage; it does not certify that text as evidence.
Decomposition can improve coverage while adding retrieval and synthesis cost.

concepts.title: Query rewrite
concepts.meaning: A transformation of a user's search wording into one or more retrieval keys that preserve the original request and its constraints.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Show one conversational question card branching into one clarified query and two compact subquery cards. Keep a thin original-query branch in parallel, and attach a separate trusted filter tag to every branch. Use a pencil or transform arrow, not a magic answer spark.
pitfalls: A rewrite is a lookup aid, not the answer.
Keep exact identifiers and the original intent available when rewrites drift.
Authorization filters must accompany every rewritten query.

sourceRefs.title: Advanced RAG: HyDE & Self-RAG
headings: What rewrite, HyDE, and CRAG can break

concepts.title: Randomized treatment
concepts.meaning: Random assignment makes the treatment and control groups comparable in expectation.
concepts.brief: Randomly assign users to control and treatment, show equal expected baselines and the observed click-through rates, then calculate risk difference, relative lift, standard error, and a confidence interval from the same counts. Reveal allocation ratio and guardrail metrics, then demonstrate how sample-ratio mismatch, repeated peeking, contamination, and noncompliance change the claim. Separate an intention-to-treat estimate from a per-protocol comparison.
pitfalls: Randomization balances measured and unmeasured baseline causes only in expectation.
A treatment effect is tied to the assigned intervention and target population.
Repeated unplanned peeking can inflate error unless a sequential design is used.
Sample-ratio mismatch is a diagnostic signal that needs investigation, not a causal effect.
Statistical significance does not establish product value or rule out guardrail harm.

concepts.title: Ranking metrics
concepts.meaning: Distinct summaries of retrieval relevance, rank position, and recall.
concepts.brief: Animate recall@k, reciprocal rank, and average precision on one list.
pitfalls: No one metric substitutes for answer quality.

sourceRefs.title: Context Engineering: Beyond Prompting
headings: Retrieve the next fact you need

concepts.title: Reasoning budget tree
concepts.meaning: Inference budget can fund longer reasoning, more candidates, and verification before selecting an answer.
concepts.brief: Allocate a finite budget across candidate branches, show oracle availability versus selection accuracy, and stop under explicit cost.
pitfalls: Candidate independence, verifier mistakes, correlation, and latency affect the value of additional sampling.

concepts.title: Reasoning search tree
concepts.meaning: Several partial solution paths are evaluated, pruned, and continued under a budget.
concepts.brief: Compare one linear trace, independent samples with a vote, and a bounded tree search. Show the evaluator and token budget separately from model-generated candidates.
pitfalls: Repeated sampling helps only under assumptions about candidate diversity and aggregation.
A heuristic evaluator can favor fluent but incorrect paths.

sourceRefs.title: CoT, ToT & Self-Consistency Prompting
headings: Use a problem that actually needs branching

concepts.title: Recommendation candidate slate
concepts.meaning: Eligible candidates are retrieved, scored, and assembled into an ordered recommendation slate.
concepts.brief: Filter stale or unauthorized documents, move a seven-item retrieval shortlist through a hand-authored scorer, compare ranked lists and graded gains, then apply slate constraints. Keep candidate recall separate from reranking quality, policy eligibility, and online causal measurement.
pitfalls: A ranker cannot recover a relevant item omitted from candidate generation.
Learned relevance scores never grant access to private content.
Illustrative fixture scores and funnel counts are not benchmark measurements.
Position-biased clicks and offline ranking metrics do not by themselves establish online product impact.

concepts.title: Recurrent and gated state
concepts.meaning: Carries a learned state through an ordered sequence, with LSTM/GRU gates controlling updates.
concepts.brief: Unroll three sequence steps with shared weights; trace hidden state and, for LSTM, separate cell state through forget/input/output gates. Highlight how a distant gradient travels backward.
pitfalls: Gate diagrams should distinguish LSTM and GRU equations.
A hidden state is a compressed learned representation, not a lossless transcript.

sourceRefs.title: RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and Sequence Modeling

concepts.title: Recursive context tree
concepts.meaning: A large source divides into bounded leaves and recombines through merge steps.

concepts.title: Regression residual
concepts.meaning: A residual is the vertical gap between an observed value and its fitted prediction at the same input.
concepts.brief: Place a fitted line beside observed points and animate one vertical residual from the line to its matching observation.
pitfalls: Measure residuals along the response axis at the same input coordinate.

concepts.title: Policy and environment loop
concepts.meaning: Improves a policy through repeated state, action, outcome, and reward feedback.
concepts.brief: Show a state or observation entering a policy, an action changing the environment, and the next observation and reward returning to the learner. Keep episodic return separate from one-step reward; include a replayable trajectory for the LLM case.
pitfalls: A reward function is a training signal, not a complete specification of human value.
Observed reward may arrive later than the action that produced it.

concepts.title: Release gate
concepts.meaning: Predeclared decision rule required before an artifact or system advances.
concepts.brief: Quality, safety, latency, and rollback checks converge with owners.
pitfalls: A gate does not replace monitoring.

sourceRefs.title: What Does an AI Engineer Actually Do?

concepts.title: Release manifest
concepts.meaning: A versioned identity that binds model bytes to the tokenizer, prompt, retrieval, policy, serving, and evaluation inputs that produced a live behavior.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. A central digest card connects to small chips for weights, tokenizer, prompt, retriever, policy, serving config, and eval suite. A moving alias points to the immutable manifest; a changed dependency creates a new manifest.
pitfalls: A digest identifies declared bytes and inputs only when those bytes are actually verified.
An alias can move without rewriting the manifest.
Do not treat registry presence as production deployment proof.

concepts.title: Bounded request queue
concepts.meaning: A finite waiting area for admitted work with visible age, deadline, and caller ownership.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Draw four request cards in a queue with a clear capacity boundary, per-card deadline ticks, and one worker slot at the exit. Keep one rejected request outside the queue with a retry-after badge.
pitfalls: Queue length alone is not a wait-time guarantee.
A finite queue does not replace deadlines or cancellation.
Requests need tenant ownership and fairness context.

concepts.title: Request trace
concepts.meaning: A parent request span connected to retrieval, model, tool, safety, and response spans with timestamps and stable identities.
concepts.brief: Request fans through retrieval/model/tool spans with parent links and failure location.
pitfalls: A trace describes one path, metrics aggregate populations.
Span timing does not alone prove answer quality or causal attribution.
Avoid embedding raw prompts or secrets in the symbol.
A trace is not the same as an application stack trace.

sourceRefs.title: LLM Observability & Monitoring
headings: Follow request execution with distinct spans
Distributed tracing in multi-agent trajectories and tool loops

concepts.title: Paired seed trial
concepts.meaning: Each random seed runs both arms, so the comparison uses matched within-seed differences.

concepts.title: Response token mask
concepts.meaning: Prompt tokens remain contextual input while selected response tokens receive training loss.
concepts.brief: Serialize a message with its model template, shift input tokens into next-token targets, and distinguish prompt context from assistant targets included in loss.
pitfalls: Masking prompt targets does not remove prompt tokens from contextual attention.
Target shifts and segment-start rules must align with the actual template.

sourceRefs.title: Instruction Tuning & Chat Templates
headings: Which tokens should receive the loss?

concepts.title: Retrieval fusion and reranking
concepts.meaning: Combines candidate lists from complementary retrieval methods, then spends more compute on a shortlist.
concepts.brief: Route one query through sparse lexical and dense vector lanes, merge ranked lists with a labeled fusion step, rerank a small candidate set with a joint query-document scorer, and surface evidence spans.
pitfalls: Candidate retrieval locates evidence; it does not grant permission or prove answer support.
Keep shortlist size and expensive scoring boundary visible.

concepts.title: Retrieval pipeline
concepts.meaning: Stages from candidate generation through filtering, ranking, packing, and evidence use.
concepts.brief: Lexical/dense→ACL→rerank→context→citation with failure surfaces.
pitfalls: Each stage has its own denominator; evidence may be ignored.

sourceRefs.title: Context Engineering: Beyond Prompting
headings: Test whether the evidence changes the answer

sourceRefs.title: What Does an AI Engineer Actually Do?

concepts.title: Retry with backoff and jitter
concepts.meaning: A bounded retry schedule that spreads attempts over time while preserving one operation identity and an absolute deadline.
concepts.brief: Multiple clients recover from a 503 on spread-out jittered timelines.
pitfalls: Retry only transient, retry-safe operations.
Jitter spreads retries but does not make them safe by itself.
Keep a total attempt cap and absolute deadline.
Reuse the same idempotency key when reconciling the same operation.

sourceRefs.title: Agent Reliability, Recovery & Human Approval
headings: Back off without multiplying the damage

concepts.title: Reward
concepts.meaning: A training signal that scores a candidate response.

concepts.title: Reward feedback loop
concepts.meaning: An agent observes a state, acts, receives a reward, and continues from the resulting state.
concepts.brief: Use a small stochastic navigation fixture with explicit states, actions, transition probabilities, rewards, terminal states, and discount factor. Compare a one-step bandit reward with a multi-step Markov decision process, animate a trajectory, then compute a Bellman backup and a Q-learning update from the realized transition. Show that exploration changes which evidence the agent collects and that a reward specification does not guarantee safe or useful behavior.
pitfalls: The Markov property applies to the modeled state; omitted history may make the chosen state representation insufficient.
A bandit action has no action-dependent next state in the basic formulation.
Model-free Q-learning's convergence results require specific finite tabular and exploration assumptions.
Discounting changes the objective and finite-horizon problems need terminal handling.
An optimized reward can diverge from the real objective.

concepts.title: Reward-model exploitation loop
concepts.meaning: Shows how optimizing a proxy reward can amplify behaviors that score well while missing the intended human objective.
concepts.brief: Place a target-quality axis beside proxy reward; move a policy update through examples that exploit verbosity, sycophancy, or format shortcuts, and compare proxy gains with fresh human evaluation.
pitfalls: The model can exploit evaluator correlations without an explicit intention to deceive.
Use concrete failure examples and report the evaluation distribution.

concepts.title: Risk-coverage curve
concepts.meaning: Error among accepted cases as the system accepts a larger or smaller share.
concepts.brief: Move a reject threshold and animate accepted coverage with selective error.
pitfalls: Rejected cases need a safe path.

sourceRefs.title: Context Engineering: Beyond Prompting
headings: A summary must preserve the uncertainty

concepts.title: Roofline performance model
concepts.meaning: Bounds kernel throughput by peak compute and memory bandwidth at a given arithmetic intensity.
concepts.brief: Plot arithmetic intensity on a log x-axis and attainable performance on y; draw bandwidth slope, compute ceiling, ridge point, and one labeled kernel moving across the boundary.
pitfalls: The roofline is a bound under stated hardware and measurement assumptions.
Occupancy, launch overhead, cache behavior, and synchronization can lower measured performance further.

sourceRefs.title: GEMM From Naive CUDA to Tensor Cores

concepts.title: Rotation
concepts.meaning: A phase rotation that encodes relative position in paired dimensions.

concepts.title: Router
concepts.meaning: A learned gate assigns incoming work to selected paths.

sourceRefs.title: How Decision Models Like Jev Work: AI Without the Paragraph

concepts.title: Runtime buffer lifetime
concepts.meaning: A copy-stream event orders a consumer stream, and the buffer remains alive through consumption and completion.
concepts.brief: Queue a copy on a producer stream, record a ready event and enqueue a consumer wait on another stream. Keep the allocation live through the consumer and release it only after dependent work completes.
pitfalls: A stream wait orders device work without blocking the host.
A wait on an unrecorded event represents empty prior work; record before waiting.

concepts.title: Runtime policy gate
concepts.meaning: A trusted decision point that checks caller identity, action, arguments, resource scope, and required approval before a side effect.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. A request card approaches a gate with four small checks in sequence: principal, action name, argument scope, approval. A green path reaches a tool; a red path returns a compact deny receipt. Keep the gate between request and effect.
pitfalls: Prompt wording is not the enforcement boundary.
A passing name check still needs argument and resource checks.
Detection after an effect cannot retroactively authorize it.

concepts.title: Safety policy gate
concepts.meaning: Input, action, and output checks protect different stages of a model interaction.

concepts.title: Sampler
concepts.meaning: A numerical procedure that follows a learned distribution to generate a sample.

concepts.title: Sampling distributions and bootstrap
concepts.meaning: Uses repeated samples to show how an estimator varies under finite data and dependence assumptions.
concepts.brief: Draw a population and sample, then repeatedly resample rows with replacement to form an empirical distribution for a statistic; show paired resampling and effective sample size where relevant.
pitfalls: Bootstrap validity depends on the sampling unit and dependence structure.
A narrow interval cannot repair biased or unrepresentative data.

concepts.title: Sandbox
concepts.meaning: Constrained execution limiting resources, filesystem/network access, and authority.
concepts.brief: Untrusted process inside explicit CPU/time/filesystem/network controls.
pitfalls: Containerization alone does not guarantee isolation.

sourceRefs.title: How to Build an AI Agent from Scratch
headings: Give the model a small, explicit world

concepts.title: Agent sandbox boundary
concepts.meaning: An operating-system-enforced boundary that limits an agent's filesystem, process, network, credentials, and runtime resources.
concepts.brief: 16:9 diagram. Put the untrusted worker inside a workspace or microVM boundary with allowed project paths and bounded compute. Place the supervisor, secret store, and external network outside. Show denied edges to host credentials and internal metadata services; route allowed network requests through a policy proxy.
pitfalls: A container label alone does not guarantee isolation.
Mounted host sockets, broad credentials, or unrestricted egress can defeat the boundary.
Runtime resource caps and cleanup need explicit owners.

sourceRefs.title: Design a Multi-Tenant Agent Sandbox & Code Interpreter Platform
headings: Keep the VMM's host authority small
Hardware Virtualization: Linux KVM and Firecracker Internals

concepts.title: Sandbox execution boundary
concepts.meaning: Generated code runs inside a bounded workspace separated from secrets and network paths.
concepts.brief: Keep generated code, sandbox, and trusted evaluation in distinct zones. Animate filesystem and egress gates plus CPU, memory, and time limits.
pitfalls: A sandbox limits authority but does not make untrusted code harmless.
The trusted supervisor and grading secrets stay outside the worker boundary.

sourceRefs.title: Code Generation & Sandboxing
headings: Keep the worker away from the authority to grade it

concepts.title: Scaling frontier
concepts.meaning: A scaling frontier compares achievable model quality with compute and exposes diminishing returns.
concepts.brief: Plot quality against compute on a log-scaled axis; mark the frontier knee and compare feasible training choices.
pitfalls: Label compute and avoid implying quality rises linearly forever.

concepts.title: Schema automaton
concepts.meaning: A schema automaton tracks valid output states and blocks tokens that cannot lead to a valid structure.
concepts.brief: Trace token choices through a state machine; valid transitions reach acceptance while invalid prefixes terminate.
pitfalls: The schema constrains structure; the model still chooses among allowed continuations.

concepts.title: Secret broker
concepts.meaning: A host-controlled service that performs a narrowly scoped authenticated request for an untrusted worker without exposing its credential.
concepts.brief: 16:9 diagram. A sandboxed worker submits a typed request through a local socket to a host broker. The broker verifies task scope, attaches one short-lived credential to an upstream request, sanitizes the response, and returns only safe JSON. Draw no direct worker-to-secret or worker-to-upstream path.
pitfalls: The broker still needs argument and destination policy.
A sanitized response can still contain adversarial instructions.
Never imply that a Unix socket automatically enforces authorization.

sourceRefs.title: Design a Multi-Tenant Agent Sandbox & Code Interpreter Platform
headings: Give the broker an explicit protocol

concepts.title: Secret redaction
concepts.meaning: Detection and replacement/removal of credentials before exposure or storage.
concepts.brief: Scanner replaces matched credential with typed redaction marker.
pitfalls: Pattern scans miss secrets and can redact benign text.

concepts.title: Selective affine scan
concepts.meaning: Input-dependent affine updates compose in order to recover every prefix state.
concepts.brief: Compute carry and write terms, regroup adjacent update pairs, and compare every state with the sequential reference.
pitfalls: Preserve update order, distinguish Mamba discretization from exact zero-order hold, and account for every live buffer.

concepts.title: Semantic cache eligibility
concepts.meaning: A reuse layer that returns a prior answer only after access, release, freshness, and similarity requirements all hold.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. A new query approaches a cache card through three compact gates: caller access, source freshness, and release version. Only then does a similarity lens compare it with a stored query-answer pair. Keep a bypass path when any rule fails.
pitfalls: Similarity is a candidate signal, not truth or authorization.
Cached content can be stale or cross-tenant even when vectors are close.
Cache writes need their own provenance and approval policy.

concepts.title: Semantic cache gate
concepts.meaning: A nearby question reaches a candidate answer that must pass three reuse checks.

concepts.title: Sequence packing
concepts.meaning: Packing short training sequences into one block reduces padding while keeping boundaries visible.
concepts.brief: Compare padded sequences with a packed block that places several examples contiguously and marks boundaries.
pitfalls: Packing must preserve sequence boundaries and attention/loss semantics.

concepts.title: Sequential test
concepts.meaning: Experiment analysis accounting for repeated looks at accumulating data.
concepts.brief: Evidence trajectory meets a predeclared stopping boundary.
pitfalls: Repeated ordinary fixed-sample p-values inflate false positives.

concepts.title: Serving benchmark latency
concepts.meaning: A measured serving trace separates median latency from the slower tail over a defined load interval.
concepts.brief: Grow concurrent requests against a model server, animate queue depth and token throughput, and update latency percentiles from the same authored request trace. Contrast steady-state and overload, include warmup and request length, and keep local fixture values explicitly illustrative.
pitfalls: Throughput, time to first token, inter-token latency, and end-to-end latency answer different questions.
Averages can hide tail latency; report the percentile with its sample and workload definition.
Do not present authored example timings as hardware benchmark results.
Warmup, concurrency, prompt/output lengths, batching, and error rates affect comparisons.

concepts.title: Sigmoid threshold
concepts.meaning: A probability threshold converts a logistic model score into a class decision.
concepts.brief: Plot a sigmoid probability curve against a horizontal decision threshold, then mark where an example crosses it.
pitfalls: Keep the output probability scale bounded between zero and one.

concepts.title: Singular directions
concepts.meaning: Orthogonal directions show which input variations survive a linear transformation most strongly.
concepts.brief: Map a round input cloud into an elongated output cloud; mark its orthogonal principal directions and unequal stretch factors.
pitfalls: Keep principal directions orthogonal and distinguish input from output space.

concepts.title: SLO and error budget
concepts.meaning: A measurement window and explicit good-event rule that determine how much service behavior may miss a user-facing target.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Draw a bounded 28-day window ring or short calendar strip, a numerator of good eligible requests, and a remaining error-budget gauge. Attach a tiny TTFT or success criterion tag so the metric's event boundary is visible.
pitfalls: Declare the eligible request population and good-event rule.
Averages can hide tail and slice failures.
An SLO is a target, not an automatic guarantee.

concepts.title: Softmax distribution
concepts.meaning: Turns a row of raw scores into normalized probability mass over competing choices.
concepts.brief: Place logits as signed bars, subtract the maximum, exponentiate, and normalize into a second probability row. Let temperature change how concentrated the mass becomes; keep the target token and cumulative top-p cutoff as optional overlays.
pitfalls: Probability mass alone does not establish empirical calibration.
Keep stable max-shift arithmetic visible when teaching overflow.

concepts.title: Sparse autoencoder feature view
concepts.meaning: Maps activations into a wider sparse feature space and reconstructs the original activation.
concepts.brief: Show a transformer activation vector entering an overcomplete encoder, a small set of active feature bars, and decoder contributions reconstructing the original vector; optionally visualize feature overlap in a toy 2D model.
pitfalls: Learned features are hypotheses that require validation, not automatically faithful human concepts.
Show reconstruction error and sparsity pressure together.

concepts.title: Sparse feature dictionary
concepts.meaning: A sparse code reconstructs a mixed model activation using a few learned dictionary directions.
concepts.brief: Build a known superposition, infer sparse coefficients, reconstruct it, and test a feature intervention.
pitfalls: Separate learned feature associations, reconstruction fidelity, and demonstrated causal effects. Control decoder scaling.

concepts.title: Speculative draft and verify
concepts.meaning: A draft model proposes several tokens that a larger model verifies in one parallel pass.
concepts.brief: Show draft tokens entering verification, then separate accepted tokens from the first rejected token and correction.
pitfalls: Verification uses the target model distribution; rejection can resample a corrected token.

concepts.title: SQL relational links
concepts.meaning: Foreign keys connect rows across tables so a join can recover each chunk’s source.

concepts.title: Statistical power
concepts.meaning: Probability a test detects a specified effect under a stated alternative and design.
concepts.brief: Overlay null/alternative curves, alpha/beta, sample-size effect.
pitfalls: Power is conditional on the assumed effect and design.

concepts.title: Streaming feature watermark
concepts.meaning: A streaming feature advances through event time while late arrivals remain distinguishable from on-time state.

concepts.title: Structured tool call
concepts.meaning: Typed request with schema-validated arguments and separately checked result.
concepts.brief: Proposal passes validation, authorization, execution, result normalization.
pitfalls: Valid JSON is not authorization.

sourceRefs.title: AI Engineer Portfolio Projects for Interviews
How to Build an AI Agent from Scratch
headings: Write the loop before connecting a provider

sourceRefs.title: What Does an AI Engineer Actually Do?

concepts.title: Synthetic data admission loop
concepts.meaning: Generates candidate training examples and filters them against quality, execution, safety, and diversity checks.
concepts.brief: Compose seed examples, generator, deterministic verifier, calibrated judge/human review, deduplication, and admitted dataset; show rejected rows with reasons and preserve source lineage.
pitfalls: Generated volume does not establish capability gain.
Keep contamination, recursive model collapse, and lineage risks visible.

concepts.title: Synthetic data filter
concepts.meaning: Generated examples pass quality, correctness, duplication, and diversity checks before training admission.
concepts.brief: Seed a small natural-language task set, generate variants, execute arithmetic or code checks where possible, filter duplicates and invalid candidates, then visualize admitted coverage and a held-out downstream result.
pitfalls: A fluent generation can still be false or underspecified.
A judge must be calibrated and independently audited for the task.
Recursive training can amplify generator errors and narrow the data distribution.

concepts.title: Task-vector model merging
concepts.meaning: Represents a fine-tune as a parameter difference from a shared base and combines such deltas.
concepts.brief: Place a base checkpoint as an origin, draw task vectors from it, and show weighted addition, subtraction, sign conflict, and a validation gate for a merged candidate.
pitfalls: Weight coordinates must be compatible; matching tensor shapes alone does not ensure semantic alignment.
A merged model requires fresh evaluation.

concepts.title: Teacher-student distillation
concepts.meaning: Trains a smaller student to match information from a larger teacher through soft targets, features, or generated responses.
concepts.brief: Align teacher and student token distributions at a shared temperature; show KL loss on soft logits, optional feature matching, and response-data transfer when vocabularies do not align.
pitfalls: Teacher confidence may encode errors and biases.
Token-level logit matching requires compatible vocabularies and alignment.

concepts.title: Temporal feature availability
concepts.meaning: Checks that each training/evaluation feature was available at the prediction decision time.
concepts.brief: Place prediction time, feature event time, ingestion/availability time, and label-maturity time on one entity timeline; shade only values eligible for the row and compare with a leaking future join.
pitfalls: Event timestamps alone do not prove a value was known to the system then.
Availability is row- and entity-specific.

concepts.title: Tensor axes
concepts.meaning: Coordinate axes and a tensor slice reveal how dimensions extend beyond a flat matrix.

concepts.title: Tensor shard
concepts.meaning: Tensor parallelism partitions a weight matrix across devices and combines partial results at communication boundaries.
concepts.brief: Split one weight matrix into device-owned shards, show local computation, and mark where partial results communicate.
pitfalls: Distinguish tensor shards from replicated data-parallel copies.

concepts.title: Classification threshold sweep
concepts.meaning: Shows how a decision threshold changes classifications and precision/recall trade-offs.
concepts.brief: Sort scored examples along one axis and drag a threshold; update TP/FP/FN/TN, precision, recall, and ROC or precision-recall point in sync.
pitfalls: Threshold choice depends on costs, prevalence, and operating policy.
An ROC curve can look strong under severe class imbalance.

concepts.title: Token
concepts.meaning: One discrete piece of text the model can process.

How Decision Models Like Jev Work: AI Without the Paragraph

concepts.title: Token bucket
concepts.meaning: Rate limiter with capped balance replenished over time and spent on admission.
concepts.brief: Bucket refills at r up to b; bursts pass until empty.
pitfalls: Average rate plus burst allowance, not fixed window.

sourceRefs.title: AI Lab Coding Interview: Python Systems

concepts.title: Token economics meter
concepts.meaning: Input, cached context, and generated output have separate token usage and cost weights.
concepts.brief: Trace a request's prompt, reusable cached prefix, generated output, retries, and tool steps into token and dollar cost; compute cost per successful task from an explicitly authored workload. Show how routing, batching, context trimming, and cache reuse change both cost and quality constraints.
pitfalls: Provider prices and cache discounts vary and change; cite a dated source or use clearly authored example rates.
Tokens are not words, and input, cached input, and generated output may be billed differently.
Cost per request omits retries, failures, and task success; state the denominator.
Savings must be evaluated with quality, latency, and provider-specific behavior held visible.

concepts.title: Token stream
concepts.meaning: An ordered sequence of token pieces flowing through a model.

concepts.title: Token surprisal
concepts.meaning: A model assigns log loss to observed tokens and perplexity exponentiates their average surprise.
concepts.brief: Compare token probability products through accumulated log loss, weighted corpus aggregation, and context-window scoring.
pitfalls: Match tokenization, target masking, context policy, and evaluation data before comparing perplexities.

concepts.title: Subword tokenization algorithms
concepts.meaning: Segments text into token IDs under a fixed vocabulary and tokenizer-specific rules.
concepts.brief: Put the same Unicode string through parallel BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece lanes. Reveal pair-frequency merges, greedy longest-match pieces, and Unigram alternative segmentations with IDs and detokenization.
pitfalls: Token boundaries are model-specific and part of the checkpoint contract.
Show Unicode bytes/normalization when relevant; do not imply word-like boundaries always hold.

concepts.title: Tool call envelope
concepts.meaning: A structured operation proposed by a model and executed only by a host that validates and authorizes its name and arguments.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Draw a request envelope with a tool-name chip and two argument rows, a dotted arrow entering a host boundary, and a separate observation card returning. The arrow must visibly pass through a small gate before reaching the tool icon.
pitfalls: The model proposes the call; the trusted runtime executes it.
Well-formed arguments do not imply authorization.
Tool output returns as data and remains untrusted evidence.

headings: Validate observation identity and payload schema

concepts.title: Tool protocol messages
concepts.meaning: A host and server exchange correlated request and response messages through a client.
concepts.brief: Trace discovery and a request/response exchange across host, client, and server. Keep request IDs, transport, tool errors, and protocol errors distinct.
pitfalls: Request IDs correlate messages; they do not identify conversation memory.
Protocol compatibility does not grant authorization to server capabilities.

sourceRefs.title: MCP & Tool Protocol Standards
headings: Trace the wire before hiding it behind an SDK

concepts.title: Traffic split
concepts.meaning: A weighted routing rule that sends eligible requests to different live destinations while preserving assignment identity.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Show one request stream splitting into two lanes with small percentage labels and a stable assignment pin attached to a user/session. Give each lane a distinct version marker. Ensure the icon reads as request routing rather than token fan-out.
pitfalls: Weights apply to eligible requests, not automatically to every token or every tenant.
Users may see real answers and side effects on both live arms.
A traffic share does not guarantee randomization or correct experiment units.

concepts.title: Training step loop
concepts.meaning: A minibatch cycles through forward, loss, backward, and parameter update.
concepts.brief: Track a minibatch through logits, loss, gradient accumulation, parameter update, and validation. Keep gradient clearing, backward, and optimizer step ordering visible.
pitfalls: Accumulated gradients remain until cleared.
Falling training loss alone does not establish generalization.

sourceRefs.title: PyTorch Training Loops
headings: The five execution phases in a training step

concepts.title: Training step state machine
concepts.meaning: Orders gradient reset, forward computation, loss evaluation, backward propagation, and optimizer update.
concepts.brief: Build a loop state machine with tensors, gradients, optimizer moments, and counters as persistent state; show accumulation steps joining before a single optimizer update and checkpoint boundary.
pitfalls: Gradient accumulation sums or averages gradients according to the trainer contract.
A completed microbatch is not necessarily an optimizer update.

concepts.title: Transformer block
concepts.meaning: A transformer block combines attention and a feed-forward layer with residual paths.
concepts.brief: Show token state passing through attention and feed-forward sublayers while residual routes preserve the incoming representation.
pitfalls: Keep attention and feed-forward operations sequential within one block.

concepts.title: Trust boundary
concepts.meaning: Crossing between components with different authority, identity, or data trust.
concepts.brief: Zone user/retriever/model/tool; mark enforced crossings and untrusted results.
pitfalls: Every crossing requires concrete enforcement.

concepts.title: Typed workflow state
concepts.meaning: A shared, versioned record whose fields and identities let workflow nodes exchange validated evidence without relying on free-form summaries.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Use a compact card with three typed rows: stable ID, version, and status. Add tiny source and owner badges. A second incoming update should merge into one named field rather than overwrite the whole card.
pitfalls: Do not depict a prose summary as equivalent to typed authoritative state.
A reducer must define how multiple writers merge; conflicting fields need validation.
State content does not itself grant permission.

concepts.title: Value
concepts.meaning: A value vector whose information is combined in proportion to its attention weight.

concepts.title: Variational autoencoder path
concepts.meaning: Encodes an input as a latent distribution, samples a code, and trains a decoder under reconstruction and prior-matching terms.
concepts.brief: Move a small image through encoder outputs μ and σ, sample with z=μ+σϵ, decode a reconstruction, and plot prior/posterior latent points with reconstruction and KL terms.
pitfalls: A latent point is a learned code; coordinates need not have human-interpretable meaning.
The KL term encourages prior matching but can contribute to posterior collapse.

concepts.title: Verifiable answer
concepts.meaning: An independent checker tests an answer against a defined outcome contract and emits evidence.
concepts.brief: Show a natural-language math or code task, the generated candidate, the executable or symbolic check, and its binary outcome. Sample a group of candidate answers and compute relative advantages from actual verifier scores.
pitfalls: A verifier can only check the contract it implements.
Formatting success alone does not establish correctness.
Subjective qualities need a different evaluation signal.

concepts.title: Voice turn
concepts.meaning: Incoming speech interrupts outgoing audio and updates which part of a response was heard.
concepts.brief: Use an explicitly synthetic incident-hotline trace: stream STT while the caller speaks, commit only after a complete stable identifier, overlap LLM and TTS work, then cancel queued playback on barge-in. Track which audio the client acknowledged separately from generated text.
pitfalls: Treating voice activity detection as proof that a semantic turn is complete
Adding overlapping latency spans as though they were serial
Speaking a factual tool result from an unstable partial transcript
Keeping unheard or cancelled audio in the conversation history
Presenting an illustrative timing trace as a production latency guarantee

concepts.title: Voice turn and playback state
concepts.meaning: The live voice-session state that distinguishes detected speech, committed turns, generated audio, confirmed playback, and interruption.
concepts.brief: 16:9 timeline. Show short microphone frames feeding VAD, turn commit, streaming model clauses, TTS chunks, playback acknowledgements, and a user barge-in. At interruption mute and cancel pending audio; commit only transcript text whose audio was acknowledged by the client.
pitfalls: VAD detects speech activity; endpointing decides when a turn is complete.
Generated audio is not confirmed playback.
Do not treat a network chunk timestamp as a word or token timestamp.

sourceRefs.title: Real-Time Voice AI Agent
headings: When the user interrupts: barge-in handling
The latency budget: a worked example

concepts.title: Warp reduction
concepts.meaning: GPU lanes combine partial values through synchronized parallel steps.
concepts.brief: Compute a small vector sum first, then animate warp-level pairwise shuffle steps and block partials with barriers. Compare a prefix scan that exposes every cumulative total, show floating-point tree order, and update online softmax's running maximum and rescaled sum from computed state.
pitfalls: Showing a reduction tree without calculating each intermediate value
Using warp shuffle as if it were a memory barrier
Implying blocks in an ordinary kernel can synchronize globally at an arbitrary point
Treating floating-point reassociation as exact real arithmetic
Describing Hillis-Steele and Blelloch scans without showing work and output contracts

concepts.title: Weights
concepts.meaning: Learned numerical parameters that shape a model's behavior.

sourceRefs.title: Run Gemma 4 with Ollama: Model Tags and Memory Requirements
Run Qwen3.6 Locally with llama.cpp and Unsloth GGUF

concepts.title: Workflow checkpoint
concepts.meaning: A durable snapshot of execution position and pending-operation identity used to resume after interruption and reconcile external effects.
concepts.brief: 64x64 SVG. Show a small workflow node paused beside a durable disk marker. Store the node ID, state version, and idempotency key as tiny labeled rows. On resume, a read arrow checks the external operation receipt before the effect path continues.
pitfalls: A checkpoint does not prove an external write failed or succeeded.
Resume must inspect the external operation and reuse its identity.
A framework replay must not repeat an unprotected side effect.

sourceRefs.title: Agent Reliability, Recovery & Human Approval
headings: Restore workflow checkpoints and reconcile external effects

concepts.title: Workflow DAG
concepts.meaning: A directed workflow in which independent tasks can fan out, validated results join, and external effects have explicit owners.
concepts.brief: 16:9 diagram. A single proposal node fans out to three read-only checks. Each produces an identity-bound typed receipt; a fan-in barrier validates all receipts, then pauses for approval before one writer node. Animate independent branches concurrently and serialize the final effect.
pitfalls: A workflow DAG is not the same as every graph or state machine.
Parallel reads do not imply safe parallel writes.
An explicit retry inside a node does not automatically add a graph cycle.

concepts.title: Workflow state machine
concepts.meaning: Named states and guarded transitions constraining progress and recovery.
concepts.brief: Graph guards/checkpoints/retries; animate legal and rejected transition.
pitfalls: Retries can repeat effects without idempotency.

sources.title: Production RAG Pipelines
basis: Checked document-chunk: Chunks retain document/version/parent/span identity, and small-child search expands into sufficient parent context rather than treating the chunk as a detached page crop.
Checked citation-span: The typed evidence record retains character offsets, source version and claim support; existence of a citation/span is explicitly separated from entailment and current access.

Checked access-filter: Trusted caller/tenant/document/release predicates remove forbidden records before candidate ranking or prompt packing. The tempting forbidden hit remains denied even if it would rank highest.
Checked evidence-packet: The bounded pack keeps ordered IDs, version, locator and enough supporting text. The maximum token budget can remain underfilled, and insufficient support yields abstention.

Checked runtime-policy-gate: A trusted read-authority check binds caller and resource before evidence reaches generation; later permission changes invalidate cached evidence. This is the retrieval/read scope of the gate, not an approval mechanism for arbitrary write tools.

Checked request-trace: The actual request trace binds stages to a request identity, timings, retrieval/answer decisions and versions; evidence is redacted rather than placing raw customer material in spans.

Checked latency-waterfall: A single-clock stage budget distinguishes serial and overlapping work and keeps component timings separate from the complete request tail; component p95 values are not added as a request p95.

Checked evaluation-gate: The frozen set checks retrieval, grounded answer/abstention and authorization/critical slices before rollout; the report's local evidence does not imply unperformed service integration.

Checked evidence-retrieval-pipeline: Source/version/span identities survive access filtering, retrieval, packing and final claim-support checks; a ranked but insufficient pack does not force an answer.

sources.title: Reward Modeling from Preference Data
basis: Checked reward: The scalar score is an executed/head-computed training proxy for a completed response, not a truth probability or a release verdict.
Checked preference: Chosen/rejected answers share a prompt and annotation contract. Prompt-level grouping and repeated votes preserve the comparison identity and expose annotation noise.
Checked model: The final unmasked hidden state feeds a shared scalar head; retaining the actual trained head and its base/tokenizer/template defines the saved function.

Checked preference-training-pipeline: Chosen-minus-rejected scores become a sigmoid/BCE objective and actual CPU feature-head updates; the two-feature confounded versus controlled fit distinguishes training rank from held-out behavior.

Checked reward-hacking-loop: Length/format shortcuts raise proxy scores while violating the intended approval rule. Fresh-output and independent source checks preserve the separate failure even under unanimous scorers.
